addressing-plan.md.text:
# Memory addressing and small-set diagnostic

Authorized continuation of the failed delta-memory pilot. Diagnose the existing learned controller before changing the architecture. Do not modify model.py, associative.py, config, training or inference math. No fresh held-out claims or new model-test scoring.

1. New src/mlm/addressing.py traces a prompt through the actual model one input byte at a time, beginning with BOS. From the actual returned graph state, independently reconstruct base pooling and learned key/query/value/write gate, old-matrix read, updated matrix and normalized output logits. Validate against actual state/logits and full-prompt uninstrumented forward to float32 tolerance. The helper accepts only prompt text and frozen neural state/config; no facts/expected answers. Padding is not used by this prompt-only tracer.
2. Exact conditional read decomposition: with A_j=I−beta_j k_j k_jᵀ, r_t=sum_{s<t} beta_s(q_tᵀ A_{t-1}...A_{s+1}k_s)v_s. Compute coefficients by traversing writes backward and propagating q through each symmetric A. Exclude current/future writes. Coefficients are signed, not probabilities; raw cosine is not an overwrite-aware attribution. Compare reconstructed recall vector against actual old-matrix read.
3. Trace first8 training questions (the first full assignment/query/order case) from data/kv-binding-v1/diverse on the failed full-pilot delta checkpoint and its saved initial-delta checkpoint. Fixed selection, no cherry-picking. Offline canonical-fact regions annotate writes after inference: BOS/header/fact1/fact2/question/assistant header. Validate every byte is covered. Report mean write gates, sums of absolute/signed effective coefficients and projected contribution norms per region; these are conditional diagnostics, not causal proof of where knowledge lives. Compare query/read vectors across fixed-context query swaps. Fact metadata never enters the model/tracer.
4. Frozen readout ablation: copy params in memory, set only memory_gain=0, no retraining. Score all512 original pilot training questions with unchanged neural scorer and full English development32 stories. Compare prediction flips, correct-choice score margins, complete-group rankings, answer-only training NLL and English loss. Original checkpoints/config/data remain unchanged. This disables memory output, not writes or compute. It diagnoses coadapted channel dependence, not architectural superiority. No changed test answers, generated repairs or inference parser.
5. Independent source-matched probes: graph versus delta on one training group and four training groups, taking the first4/16 original training records/questions. Four groups cover the same entity pair with two complementary color pairs and both fact orders. Every trial resets from the same original English-only checkpoint, never from the failed pilot or another probe, with fresh optimizer, same split rates/seed42,500 QA +500 English rehearsal updates (four trials total4,000 optimizer updates). One-group exposure500, four-group exposure125 per group. Tiny validation is the first8 complete conditions from the old pilot's validation pool; no test files are created or opened. It is an exploratory debug set, not confirmation.
6. For each trained delta probe, trace its fixed first training group, and repeat readout ablation on its training set and English development. Include baseline probe train/English results. Save all sources/initial fingerprints/sampler traces/counters/config/environment/checkpoints/raw scores. Fixed endpoints, no sweeps or checkpoint promotion. Test math, actual-forward reconstruction, exclusion of future/current writes, region coverage and ablation immutability. Reuse existing tested plasticity_run; add no training/inference behavior changes. Independent review and regression/static checks before freezing.

Freeze prior checkpoint/data/config and all relevant code hashes before diagnosis/training. Outputs results/addressing/report.md +summary.json +traces and source/test/config/lock snapshots; update research.md/prd.md/README/data notes. Preserve frozen plan and all prior model artifacts. A fitted tiny training set cannot demonstrate general binding. Finite-budget failure cannot prove capacity limits. Further changes selected from these diagnostics need fresh confirmation.

plasticity-plan.md.text:
# Shared/node learning-rate and rehearsal study

Approved continuation after the equal-exposure control. Isolate acquisition and retention on the promising hierarchical pipeline without changing the graph, node update or readout.

Use its own frozen English checkpoint, the same nested 16-group subset of scratch-binding-v1, seed42, batch4/unroll128 and2,000 QA updates. Independent fresh optimizer per arm, fixed initial/final evaluations, no test files or endpoint selection. Six arms: high uniform rate0.003; low uniform rate0.0003; split base0.003 with representation/shared multiplier0.1, node multiplier1 and router multiplier1. Each rate policy has task-only and 1:1 English-rehearsal variants. Rehearsal adds2,000 English updates from the cached training stream; it costs extra compute and is not a compute-matched improvement. QA and English counters, streams and carries remain separate.

Parameter roles are explicit. Node-specific input_kernel, hidden_kernel, gru_bias and read_kernel are fast. Embedding, shared message matrix, normalization and vocabulary head are shared representations. Router group/child kernels/biases have their own rate, fast in this study. Attention readout parameters, if present, are shared. Unknown parameter names fail closed. No hardcoded answer logic is introduced.

Implement opt-in Config.shared_lr_scale, node_lr_scale, router_lr_scale (finite, positive, at most1, default1) and scale completed AdamW updates per role after global clipping/moment estimation. Scale decoupled weight decay with the effective learning rate too. Preserve the existing AdamW state structure and exact default behavior; rebuilding from config must restore split rates after checkpoint load. Standard stream resume already rejects non-stream experimental metadata. Do not modify graph/model, old artifacts or old configs.

Tests first: per-role effective update ratios including decay, legacy default equivalence, unknown-role guard, finite scale validation and checkpoint continuation equivalence. Tiny runner integration must verify independent source reset, exact QA/English updates, sampled group trace, English carry/stream snapshot, metadata and source preservation. Then lint/type/full regression checks. Review new logic before freezing the experiment. Frozen protocol includes source/config/data/all relevant training code and old exposure baseline. Re-run high/task from scratch and compare parameter fingerprints against the previous exposure endpoint to audit unchanged defaults.

Runner: src/mlm/plasticity_run.py. Dedicated fresh-only CLI with declared group count, budget, config/source and optional rehearsal. Save initial/final scored items, raw fixed samples, metrics, final/latest checkpoints, all sampled group IDs, role counts/rates, optimizer config, parameter drift, counters and initial/source hashes. Report only initial/final development and English metrics; progress counters every500 do not select checkpoints. One seed, narrow grammar, development reuse and own-architecture source remain limits.

Deliver results/plasticity/report.md and summary.json, checkpoint/source/input/trace audits and source/test/config/lock snapshots. Update research.md, prd.md and README.md with actual outcomes. Preserve frozen plan; record execution status separately. No test claims, growth, curriculum, arbitrary-device or Transformer-superiority claims follow from this experiment.

Predeclared joint diagnostic gate: at least14/16 complete training groups and English development loss no more than1.25 times the initial source loss. This gate measures acquisition plus retention only; development transfer and independent confirmation remain separate requirements. It does not select or promote a model.

hierarchy-plan.md.text:
# Hierarchical recurrent update routing prototype

Authorized: prototype four groups of two small recurrent networks, compare with the current graph, and assess whether evidence supports a Transformer replacement. Current answer: no replacement claim; no direct Transformer baseline, broad language benchmark, scaling study or controlled device runtime evidence exists.

Keep all eight GRUs, width 64, fixed bounded message graph and sum readout. Add config node_update=dense|uniform|hierarchical (default dense), groups=4, router_balance=0.01. Hierarchical root gate selects group probabilities and conditional child gates select node probabilities from current byte embedding concatenated with mean previous node state. Their product is a distribution over eight nodes. Within each GRU round blend h_new = p_i*GRU_candidate + (1-p_i)*h_old. Fixed-uniform control uses p_i=1/8; dense uses p_i=1. This distinguishes learned routing from simply slowing memory updates. There are no assigned grammar categories, POS parser, inference label lookup, dynamic growth or learned topology. Existing graph supplies bounded within/cross connections; changing topology is deliberately excluded from this first test.

Both router layers start with zero weights/biases, so hierarchical and uniform controls initially match exactly after copying shared parameters. Root/child parameters must receive finite nonzero gradients. Hierarchical adds 1,548 parameters at width64/groups4/nodes8; memory state remains 512 floats. Soft routing still computes all nodes and cannot establish sparse speed gains. Auxiliary balance loss is 0.01*(N*sum(mean_probability_i^2)-1), with padding excluded; mean routing usage/entropy and write mass are reported separately from byte prediction loss. This encourages balanced usage but does not prove useful specialization.

Preserve legacy defaults, forward/checkpoint/generation interfaces; optional return_routes=True exposes route probabilities only for this trainer/diagnostics. Test probability normalization, two-level factorization, uniform equivalence, partial memory retention, causality, resets/padding/chunk equivalence, gradients, parameter delta, default checkpoints and config validation. Standard stream warm starts must reject update-mode mismatches; experimental warm-start copies shared weights and initializes router extras.

Fresh role-balanced data via confirmation_data seed override 920231; old default seed unchanged. Same English source runs/english-v1/best.mlm for all three arms, fresh optimizers, LR0.001, batch4, unroll128. Each arm receives 1,000 QA updates plus 1,000 explicit English updates, identical QA/English stream order, evaluation every250 QA cycles. Same data, budget and base parameters; initial inference differs with update rate. No English feasibility constraint is inherited from the last study: select only by macro eight-condition known/new-name development accuracy, then QA development loss, exact ties earlier. English dev monitored separately, source reference recorded. Initial eligible. No sweeps/resume. Auxiliary balance is training-only; language metrics remain pure prediction loss.

Freeze source/config/data/code hashes before training; lock all selected hashes before fresh test. Evaluate balanced known/new-name, within/cross, both sentence orders, English retention and route utilization. Store all negative results. Runtime is uncontrolled, soft routing dense, parameters unequal: no replacement, speed, memory-efficiency or superiority claim. Cite established hierarchical MoE rather than claiming its principle is novel. Update research, PRD and usage after measured results.


Execution complete: dense, uniform-slow and learned hierarchical arms each train 1,000 QA +1,000 English updates with matched streams. All selected models score 0/144 complete test cases. English losses: 1.119035 dense, 1.953038 uniform, 1.473429 hierarchical. Router parameters and usage change, but no binding benefit or grammar specialization is demonstrated. All 54 tests and static checks pass; source snapshots are preserved. No sparse speedup, growing topology, or Transformer replacement claim is justified. Initialization mismatch and absence of a flat learned-router control remain limitations. See results/hierarchical-routing/report.md.

confirmation-plan.md.text:
# Balanced binding confirmation and explicit English rehearsal

Authorized next research step: fix the discovered pair-role imbalance, increase name diversity, keep the sum-readout graph unchanged, and explicitly test retention. This is a fresh experiment, not a silent replacement of the previous test.

Generate 64 deterministic three-letter pronounceable entity labels: 32 training, 16 new development, 16 new test. Role A/B classes are random offline strata, never model inputs. Training uses 64 entity pairs from two within-role cycles and two cross-role matchings, excluding held-out familiar-name development/test pairs. All training names have four partners; 32 pairs are within-role and 32 cross-role. Each pair gets two disjoint color pairs covering all four colors and both sentence orders. Training has 256 four-question groups / 1,024 documents. Each familiar-name evaluation pool uses 16 disjoint pairs covering all 32 training names, half within-role and half cross-role. New-name pools use eight pairs covering all 16 new names, also balanced. All six color pairs and both sentence orders are evaluated. Development/test pairs and exact text are disjoint; new-name pools are disjoint. Names are not guaranteed globally unseen in English pretraining.

Use runs/english-v1/best.mlm (original English graph) as the common source, fresh optimizer, seed 42, LR 0.001, batch four, unroll 128. Source is intentionally different from the prior memorization source: this study asks whether a clean English model can acquire binding while retaining its English. Comparisons with prior runs cannot isolate dataset balancing alone.

Both arms receive the same 2,000 complete-group QA updates in the same sampler order. Task-only gets those 2,000 optimizer updates. Rehearsal interleaves one full-document English training-stream chunk after each QA update, for 4,000 optimizer updates total. Adam state is shared across the two objectives in the rehearsal arm; recurrent state is separate, with independent QA resets and English stream carry detached across chunks. This matches task exposure, not total compute, input bytes, or update count. Both losses are mean target cross-entropy per batch; alternating steps are not a guarantee of equal gradient contribution. No story targets are secretly mixed into QA documents.

Evaluate at initial state and every 500 QA updates. Primary binding measure: macro-average of complete eight-condition correctness across familiar-name and new-name development buckets, each including both fact orders; target QA loss breaks ties. Save best-task.mlm without an English constraint. Save best.mlm only when English development loss <=1.25 times the initial English development loss, using the same binding/loss ordering. Initial state is eligible and provides the protected fallback. English TEST is not opened until checkpoint locks; development is used for the retention constraint. Report selected steps, task and total optimizer counts, actual per-objective bytes/chunks, and source identity. No resume support claimed; refuse nonempty output directories.

Freeze data/config/source/code hashes before training and lock all selected checkpoints before testing. Report protected and unconstrained checkpoints separately, identify step-zero fallbacks explicitly, and score familiar/new-name and within/cross strata. Use untouched new task test samples and the reused English test as a retention diagnostic. Record raw greedy samples separately from neural candidate ranking. One seed, artificial names, four colors and shared grammar do not establish broad language understanding. No hyperparameter sweep or architecture change.

Tests cover balanced partition counts, degree/partner coverage, pair/text/name disjointness, all eight conditions and unroll/mask bounds, protected selection, source preservation, objective counters and fresh-output guard. Implement confirmation_data.py and confirmation_run.py using existing neural training/scoring utilities. Save results and update research/PRD/README with actual outcomes and limitations.


Execution complete: both 2,000-QA arms finished; rehearsal additionally completed 2,000 English updates. All four selected checkpoints were locked and source/selection/exposure audited before testing. All score zero complete binding cases (0/96 familiar, 0/48 new). English test loss is 1.087839 rehearsal versus 1.121557 source; unconstrained task-only worsens to 3.381755 and its protected slot falls back to source. Rehearsal policy slots have identical parameters and are labelled as one trained model. All 50 tests/static checks pass. Preserve negative evidence and distinguish this new-source acquisition setting from the prior toy-transfer protocol. See results/balanced-confirmation/report.md.

data/README.md.text:
# Data used in MLM experiments

`smoke/` is an original sentence-template fixture.

`hf/` contains bounded downloads from public Hugging Face datasets and is excluded from version control. Source rows, URLs, byte/content hashes, observed Hub revisions, and local split details are in `hf/manifest.json`. The dataset viewer serves current rows; the observed Hub SHA is not a claim that the viewer request was revision-pinned. Cached response bytes preserve the exact local snapshot.

- English: [roneneldan/TinyStories](https://huggingface.co/datasets/roneneldan/TinyStories), dataset-card license CDLA-Sharing-1.0. 1,000 training stories and 32 development / 32 test stories selected from upstream validation.
- Conversation: [HuggingFaceTB/everyday-conversations-llama3.1-2k](https://huggingface.co/datasets/HuggingFaceTB/everyday-conversations-llama3.1-2k), dataset-card license Apache-2.0. 300 training conversations and 32 development / 32 test conversations selected from upstream test_sft.

Upstream held-out rows are partitioned into local development and test subsets after exact-document deduplication against training. Development chooses checkpoints; local test scores are reported after selection. This does not guarantee absence of semantic duplicates or establish performance on the full source datasets. Selection uses bounded first rows rather than a representative random sample.

JSONL preserves original story paragraphs and full conversations. Conversations use textual `<|user|>`, `<|assistant|>`, and optional `<|system|>` delimiters. These are byte sequences, not additional vocabulary tokens. The objective predicts all text, including user turns; it is not assistant-only supervised loss.

The adaptation mix uses all 300 conversations and the first 250 training stories. Both held-out domains are included in the mixed development and test sets. Story rehearsal is an explicit training strategy, not proof that forgetting is solved.

Prepare a fresh snapshot:

```sh
uv run python -m mlm.hfdata --out data/hf --stories 1000 --conversations 300 --development-size 32
```

The command also creates the mixed-stage files. Existing prepared datasets should be reused; choose a different output directory to collect another snapshot. Source licenses and attribution remain applicable; downloading does not relicense the data. No dataset has been uploaded or published by this project.


The separate `assistant-v2/` experiment is prepared by `python -m mlm.supervised_data` from verified cached public rows. It uses 64 conversations and 64 stories plus offline synthetic paired reading examples. Public source attribution/licenses above still apply. Its manifest records exact files, counts, and hashes. Reading labels are dataset-generation logic only, never inference logic.

Optional JSONL `loss_spans` contain sorted, nonoverlapping half-open UTF-8 byte ranges; `score_eos` separately enables the EOS target. Assistant records supervise assistant content/newline and the final EOS. Prompt bytes still update memory. Stories retain full-text supervision. Without spans, the historical all-target objective applies. Names and templates are disjoint across supervised reading splits, not guaranteed unseen in prior English pretraining. See [measured outcomes](../results/assistant-learning/report.md).


`retrieval-v1/` is a separate offline controlled-task dataset prepared by `python -m mlm.retrieval_data`. It contains 960 synthetic training records, 480 development records, and 480 test records, plus 32 cached public training stories in full-stage training. Basic subsets contain 64/32/32 single-fact/no-delay documents. Synthetic supervision uses assistant-only UTF-8 byte spans and EOS; stories use full-text targets. Public story attribution and license information above remain applicable.

Task names are disjoint across splits; sentence grammar and four color values are shared intentionally. Filler lengths are exactly 0/64/128 bytes. Context swaps and query swaps are grouped to expose incorrect entity selection. This is not a natural-language chat benchmark. Facts/labels in question JSON are grading metadata only; the model receives the textual prompt, and inference has no symbolic answer lookup. File hashes and bounded public-source provenance are recorded in the manifest. See [experiment details](../results/retrieval-curriculum/report.md).


`binding-v1/` is an original focused two-person dataset, prepared by `python -m mlm.binding_data`. It has 960 training documents / 240 four-question groups, 224 development / 56 groups, and 224 test / 56 groups. All unordered entity pairs within each split appear, with both fact orders; color pairs cycle through six combinations in seeded shuffled entity-pair order. Split names are disjoint within this task. Grammar and colors are shared deliberately; this does not test broad wording transfer.

`binding_run` batches all four context/query swaps together and trains on assistant-only spans plus EOS. There is no story rehearsal in this diagnostic. Its labels/factual metadata are offline training/evaluation data, never an inference solver. Dataset/source hashes and pre-test checkpoint locks are in [the focused report](../results/focused-binding/report.md). Its post-hoc single-group overfit check is training-only and must not be mixed with held-out results.


`gradual-v1/`, prepared by `python -m mlm.gradual_data`, has a nested 64-group training pool (256 documents) and two separate development/test transfer buckets: new pairs of training-pool names and names absent from the task's training pool. Each evaluation bucket has 48 four-question groups / 192 questions, or 24 cases when requiring both fact orders together. Familiar-name pair identities are disjoint across training/development/test; names intentionally overlap for that bucket. New-name development/test pools are disjoint from each other and training. The first group matches the stored single-group sanity source exactly.

A post-hoc audit found the familiar-name development/test pair roles structurally imbalanced relative to the initial curriculum pairs. This snapshot is preserved as historical evidence; use a new role-balanced confirmation design before claiming robust transfer. [Report and split audit](../results/gradual-binding/report.md). All labels/grouping/role analysis remain offline; neural inference receives only the textual prompt.


`confirmation-v1/`, prepared by `python -m mlm.confirmation_data`, is a new role-balanced snapshot: 32 artificial training names, 1,024 training documents / 256 four-question groups, and 1,152 documents in each development/test split. Familiar-name evaluation covers all 32 training names with 16 reserved pairs; new-name pools contain 16 separate labels and eight pairs. All evaluation pairs use six color combinations and both sentence orders. Within/cross-role pairs are balanced separately in every bucket, and every training name has four partners. Role classes are random offline strata, not prompt features.

Familiar/new-name bucket sizes differ (96 versus 48 eight-condition cases), so checkpoint selection gives them equal macro weight. Source, dataset and checkpoint locks are in [the study report](../results/balanced-confirmation/report.md). No story is hidden among QA records: rehearsal uses an explicit separate cached English training stream with its own counters/carry. English development constrains one checkpoint policy; the repeatedly used English test remains a retention diagnostic. Names are disjoint within the task, not guaranteed globally novel in pretraining.


`hierarchy-v1/` uses the same balanced confirmation generator with a new seed (920231), preserving old default seed731029 behavior. It contains fresh training/development/test names and pair assignments; counts and within/cross balance follow confirmation-v1. The hierarchy experiment freezes all three variants before opening this new test. See [protocol and results](../results/hierarchical-routing/report.md). Role classes are offline evaluation strata and are not the model's router groups or supplied linguistic labels.

`scratch-binding-v1/` is the balanced generator's seed 631204 snapshot, reserved for the from-scratch dense/hierarchical comparison. Counts and role balancing follow confirmation-v1. The English source remains the same bounded TinyStories snapshot; each architecture independently pretrains from random weights before adapting its own checkpoint. Test-only question files add exactly 64 or 128 neutral filler bytes to the zero-delay questions, without changing facts, choices or grading labels. These delayed sets are diagnostic and never used for selection. [Protocol and results](../results/from-scratch/report.md).


`transfer-v1/` contains fixed/diverse/mixed subdirectories from the original seed 904217 generator (`python -m mlm.transfer_data`). They share 16 task-training labels, disjoint familiar-name development/test pairings and separate 16-label new-name pools. Fixed has 16 training groups; diverse/mixed have 128 with identical underlying facts/queries and different renderers. Each development/test snapshot has six name/wording buckets of 48 complete eight-condition cases, totaling 2,304 questions. Heldout templates occur in neither training renderer. Model test scoring happens only after all endpoints are locked. Ground truth and role/wording metadata are offline labels, never an inference solver. [Protocol and results](../results/transfer/report.md).


`kv-binding-v1/` is transfer_data seed 638101 with the same verified pairing/name/wording split rules as transfer-v1. Only its diverse 128-group pool is trained in the [delta-memory pilot](../results/associative/report.md); generated fixed/mixed pools are unused. New checkpoints start from the preserved English-only source, with all model test scoring after both endpoint locks. Labels remain offline training/grading metadata; no entity parser or answer lookup is added to inference.


## Addressing debug subsets

`addressing-v1/groups-1` and `groups-4` copy the first4/16 aligned training records/questions from `kv-binding-v1/diverse`, without relabeling, and the first8 complete development conditions. Training uses the same Bon/Bom pair, one or two color pairs and one or both fact orders. These are previously available debugging subsets, not fresh confirmation datasets. No test files are created/opened. See `results/addressing/protocol.json` for hashes and the report for exposure limits.

results/focused-binding/report.md.text:
# Focused two-person binding

This experiment tests the smallest failed retrieval case: two people, two distinct colors, no filler. All unordered training-name pairs are represented, rather than the previous fixed query partners. Fact order, color assignment, and queried person are balanced. Each complete group contains both queried people crossed with both color assignments, so preferring the first/last fact cannot solve a group.

## Protocol

The task has 16 training names (120 entity pairs / 240 groups / 960 documents), eight new development names (28 pairs / 56 groups / 224 documents), and eight separate test names with the same counts. Each entity pair receives one cyclically assigned color pair from six combinations in a seeded shuffled entity-pair order, with both fact orders. This covers varied partners but not every possible name/color combination. Grammar and the four color words are shared across splits; names are disjoint within this task, not necessarily globally novel in earlier training.

One full four-question group forms each batch. Every synthetic document is 98 input bytes including BOS and fits the 128-byte unroll. Assistant answer/newline and EOS alone receive cross-entropy loss; prompt bytes update neural state. State resets between independent examples and groups. The model has no access to grading labels or factual metadata during inference. Offline label construction is not an answer solver.

Graph and GRU warm-start from their respective single-fact basic checkpoints with fresh optimizers. Both use seed 42, 2,000 updates, batch four, learning rate 0.0005, no story rehearsal, and evaluation at zero and every 250 updates. Selection maximizes complete development binding-group accuracy; target loss only breaks ties, and exact ties preserve the earlier step. This dedicated runner does not implement resume and refuses nonempty output directories.

The source/config/data hashes, group identities, and conditional readout policy are recorded before training. The conditional architecture experiment is permitted only if both controls remain below 90% development group accuracy. Test data is not used to choose this branch. All selected checkpoint hashes must be locked before first focused-test scoring.

Two-choice likelihood ranking and raw greedy generation are distinct measures. Independent random two-choice predictions average 50% individual, 25% complete context pairs, and 6.25% complete four-question groups; these are reference rates, not a significance test. Report wrong flips as well as correct groups. English retention uses the repeatedly inspected story diagnostic and is not a fresh generalization benchmark.

## Reproduction

Use fresh output paths and preserve source checkpoints.

```sh
uv run python -m mlm.binding_data --out data/binding-new
uv run python -m mlm.binding_run --data data/binding-new --config configs/binding-graph.json --init runs/retrieval-basic-graph-v1/best.mlm --out runs/focused-binding-graph-new --steps 2000 --eval-every 250
uv run python -m mlm.binding_run --data data/binding-new --config configs/binding-gru.json --init runs/retrieval-basic-gru-v1/best.mlm --out runs/focused-binding-gru-new --steps 2000 --eval-every 250
uv run python -m mlm.retrieval_eval runs/focused-binding-graph-new/best.mlm --questions data/binding-new/test-questions.json --out results/focused-binding-graph-new.json
```

Complete all planned development experiments and lock the checkpoints before running the last command. The dataset generator defaults to seed 91827. Repeated tuning after viewing this test requires another confirmation split. This is a one-seed, bounded synthetic task; it does not establish natural-language comprehension or Transformer superiority.

## Conditional learned readout

Both controls scored zero complete development groups after 2,000 updates, triggering the single predeclared readout variant before any focused-test scoring. Its key and query transforms score the eight current recurrent node states:

q = h_0 Q; e_i = v^T tanh(h_i K + q); alpha = softmax(e); readout = sqrt(N) sum_i alpha_i (h_i R_i).

Node zero supplies the conditioning state because it started with the shortest nominal retention prior. It is not an explicit question encoder, and its state is not guaranteed to represent only the query. This builds on established [additive attention](https://arxiv.org/abs/1409.0473); it is a research adaptation, not a new attention principle. Graph message aggregation remains fixed. No stored token-history attention, growing nodes, or structural routing was added.

The optional configuration is `node_readout: "attention"`; default `"sum"` retains the original path and legacy checkpoint behavior. A zero initial score vector yields uniform alpha and reproduces the old sum/sqrt(N) pooling when shared parameters are copied. The variant adds 8,256 learned parameters: 374,978 total against graph's 366,722 and GRU's 368,210. Its recurrent state remains 512 scalars per example; GRU uses 208. It is not a parameter- or compute-matched superiority test.

The dedicated grouped runner supports copying shared source tensors into a model with new readout parameters. Ordinary stream initialization requires matching readout configurations and rejects incompatible parameter trees. The new tests verify uniform equivalence, nonzero gradients, source integrity, padding, resets, causality, chunk state, config validation, and checkpoint roundtrip. Readout activity auditing confirms all three new parameter tensors changed during training. On the first test group weights remain fairly diffuse, with query-swap weight differences about 0.005 in L2 norm; that is a narrow diagnostic, not an established explanation of failure.

## Results

All three models completed 2,000 updates on the same complete-group order, consuming 776,000 input payload bytes and 40,000 supervised payload bytes each. Final sampler order, cursor, epochs, RNG, group identities, and supervision hashes match. Config, data, source and selected checkpoint hashes were checked. The graph selects step 1,750; GRU and readout variant select step 2,000. Every development group score remains zero, so the secondary loss criterion decides among eligible checkpoints. There was no test-based checkpoint choice.

| Model | Individual test answers /224 | Complete context pairs /112 | Complete binding groups /56 | Complete training groups /240 | Story test loss |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Graph, sum readout | 115 | 12 | 0 | 0 | 7.439665 |
| Plain GRU | 121 | 18 | 1 | 7 | 8.119605 |
| Graph, learned readout | 111 | 10 | 0 | 1 | 7.668399 |

Individual accuracy is 51.34%, 54.02%, and 49.55%. These results do not demonstrate reliable binding or a readout improvement. The training diagnostics evaluate the selected models on all training questions; they are not generalization results. Poor training-group performance shows that novel held-out names alone do not explain the failure. This does not prove the architectures incapable of learning binding under other optimization or data conditions.

Raw greedy generation is preserved for the fixed first complete test group (four samples per model). That tiny sample must not be presented as a full-test generation score. The complete neural likelihood scores and all correct/incorrect query/context swaps are saved in the test JSON files. No answer extraction or repair occurs.

Held-out assistant-target losses are 0.117465, 0.116768, and 0.116877. Low byte loss is misleading here: for illustration, uncertainty between two color words with distinct first bytes can contribute log(2)/6 = 0.1155 average loss over four color bytes, newline and EOS, while all later teacher-forced targets are easy. This is an explanatory reference calculation, not a fitted model of these networks' internals.

Removing rehearsal deliberately made the task objective explicit, but English prediction worsened sharply. Earlier basic-stage story losses were 3.487491 graph and 4.133074 GRU, and original English checkpoints were 1.121557 and 1.098890. None of these focused checkpoints replaces a preserved English/chat reference. The story set is a reused retention monitor. This one-seed experiment changes data pairing, batching, objective mix and selection relative to the previous curriculum, so it cannot attribute failure or improvement to one factor alone. Timing is uncontrolled and does not support speed claims.

## Training-only learnability check

After the main test was recorded, a separate post-hoc diagnostic trained the original sum-readout graph on just one four-question training group for 500 updates with learning rate 0.003 and fresh optimizer, starting from the same basic graph source. It reaches all four correct neural rankings and one complete correct binding group. This is a fixed single diagnostic, not a hyperparameter sweep or an additional model selected on the held-out test. Its scope is memorization, not generalization. The smaller dataset and higher learning rate changed together, so the result does not identify the sole cause of earlier failure.

Raw greedy generation on those same four memorized training questions scores 100%; unedited outputs are in single-group-generation.json. The sanity checkpoint is stored separately under runs/binding-overfit-sanity-v1 and is not promoted as a language model upgrade.

## Decision and verification

Keep the learned readout as an optional experimental feature, not the default. The graph can fit a tiny binding case, but the broader training protocol does not learn a useful rule. Next use a gradual curriculum from one group to multiple names/pairings, with known-name novel-pair evaluation separated from held-out-name evaluation. Fix optimization and supervision accounting before increasing capacity, and freeze new confirmation data before tuning. More graph nodes or growing topology are not yet justified by these results.

All 44 tests pass, plus Ruff lint/format and source type checks. Source checkpoints remain intact; no answers are hardcoded into inference. Offline data construction, grouping and answer keys are training/evaluation infrastructure. The optional input-dependent readout changes activations, while learned parameters remain fixed during ordinary inference; it does not implement online weight updates or node growth.

results/focused-binding/protocol.md.text:
# Focused two-person binding experiment

Approved next step: isolate one distractor, zero filler, varied name pairings and fact order, with complete context/query groups as the primary development metric. Keep graph and GRU controls. No inference solver.

Data: all unordered pairs of 16 training names, plus separate eight-name development and test pools. Each pair gets one of six unordered color pairs, cycling in shuffled entity-pair order, with both fact orders. Each order has four questions: two swapped color assignments crossed with two queried people. Each update consumes one complete group of four examples, using assistant-only byte loss and EOS. No story rehearsal in this diagnostic; measure English retention separately. This removes the previous unaccounted supervision imbalance. Grammar and four known four-byte colors are shared intentionally. Names are disjoint within this task, not globally novel.

Train from the corresponding basic-stage single-fact checkpoints, not previous binding/test-selected weights. Fresh optimizer, seed 42, batch four, unroll 128, learning rate 0.0005, 2,000 updates; evaluate at zero and every 250. Select by highest complete binding-group accuracy, then lowest assistant-target development loss; exact ties keep the earlier checkpoint. Every example fits one unroll. Shuffle groups, not individual documents. Save byte counters and sampler identity. No resume support claimed by this dedicated runner; refuse nonempty output directories.

If both controls have not demonstrated the intended binding and graph development group accuracy is below 90%, run one predetermined graph readout variant at the same budget before opening test data. Variant: additive learned node attention conditioned on node zero's recurrent state (the initially fastest-retention node), with keys from all current nodes. It is state-conditioned, not an explicit parsed question encoder. Initialize attention scores to zero so uniform weighting reproduces the old pooled readout when shared weights are copied. Scaling sqrt(nodes) preserves the old sum/sqrt(nodes) convention. Extra parameters must be reported; this is not a parameter-matched architecture comparison. It neither adds per-token Transformer attention nor growing topology. Decision depends only on development, not test.

Implement offline binding_data.py, grouped binding_run.py, and regression tests first. Test complete/varied group construction, labels and masks, shuffled full-group batches, input limits, selection priority, source integrity and output protection. Conditional readout requires uniform-equivalence, gradients, causality, padding/reset/chunk-state, and checkpoint tests before training. Preserve default sum behavior and legacy checkpoints.

Freeze data/source/config/protocol hashes before training. Lock all selected checkpoint hashes before first focused-test evaluation. Reuse frozen neural likelihood evaluator; report group accuracy, pair accuracy, wrong flips, all examples, fixed raw greedy samples and English retention. Record negative results and limitations, update research.md, prd.md and README. One seed and a small synthetic grammar cannot establish general language understanding. No git repository is present.

results/assistant-learning/report.md.text:
# Assistant-only learning experiment

Date: 2026-10-23. Outcome: the training objective and answer format improved; the reading-comprehension objective was not achieved.

## Implemented behavior

Input validity and target supervision are separate. Prompt bytes update recurrent memory; their next-byte targets do not contribute to chat/QA loss. Assistant spans are computed offline from structured roles using UTF-8 byte offsets. Newline and EOS targets are explicit. Story rehearsal retains the ordinary full-text language-model loss.

A chunk with zero supervised targets advances recurrent state while preserving parameters, optimizer moments, and optimizer step. Checkpoints preserve data and supervision hashes, masks, per-lane offsets, shuffle RNG, optimizer, and recurrent carry. Changing masks on unchanged text is rejected on resume.

Validation selection now uses global optimizer-step multiples. Off-grid endpoint evaluations are logged without competing for best. Relocating resume preserves the source best checkpoint. Incompatible legacy off-grid best states are rejected. Prefix training/evaluation rejects explicit supervision; use stream-train and full-document evaluation.

## Data and fixed protocol

The generated reading task covers color ownership and object locations with a distractor entity and varying fact order. There are 800 unique balanced training pairs / 1,600 reading examples, and 64 pairs / 128 examples each for development and test. Names and wording templates are disjoint within this supervised stage. This does not mean the names were absent from earlier English pretraining.

Short QA examples are repeated eight times explicitly. The training mix contains 12,800 QA records, 64 cached public conversations with assistant-only spans, and 64 English stories for full-text rehearsal. The manifest records counts, source hashes, and frozen suites. The preliminary assistant-v1 preparation contained duplicate pairs; it was corrected before any training. Only assistant-v2 was trained.

Offline generation rules create supervised labels. Those rules are never called by model inference. Frozen candidate scoring receives prompts and all choices, not correct-answer indices. Greedy generation receives no choices or answer key. The original reading-v1 suite was not used for training or selection and its hash remained unchanged.

Both graph and parameter-matched GRU start from their respective 4,000-update English checkpoints with fresh optimizers. Both receive 2,000 additional supervised updates, seed 42, batch size four, unroll 256, learning rate 0.0005, the same optimizer settings, and selection every 500 updates. Final sampler snapshots, corpus hashes, consumed bytes, and supervision hashes/counts match. This is one seed, not a statistical architecture ranking.

## Results

Answer loss scores assistant-target bytes and EOS. It is not comparable to the earlier full-text NLL as an improvement percentage.

| Model | Selected update | Held-out answer loss, nats | Two-choice accuracy | Both-in-pair accuracy | Greedy exact accuracy, first 16 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| graph | 1000 | 0.234342 | 50% | 0% | 12.5% |
| gru | 1500 | 0.244349 | 50% | 0% | 37.5% |

Before this stage, both English checkpoints scored 50% two-choice accuracy, 0% pair accuracy, and 0/16 exact greedy answers on the new task. After training, both still ranked the same candidate within every pair. Both also remained at 50% / 0% on the unchanged original reading suite. The familiar training-style subset also scored 50% / 0%; this is a training-data diagnostic, not a generalization result.

Raw generation became short task words. On the fixed 16-question subset, graph outputs were eight `red` and eight `bag` replies; the GRU produced category-specific `green`, `white`, and `box` defaults. The apparent 2/16 and 6/16 exact matches do not establish context use. No regex answer extraction, favorable stochastic sampling, or answer-key response rule was used. Surrounding whitespace and case are normalized only for grading.

See the complete before/after evaluation JSON files and raw greedy samples in this directory. Candidate ranking uses scorer version 2, scores answer bytes only, and uses identical chat formatting across models and stages.

## English retention

| Model | Before story test loss | After story test loss |
|---|---:|---:|
| graph | 1.121557 | 1.267662 |
| gru | 1.098890 | 1.169831 |

Story prediction worsened despite bounded rehearsal. The new checkpoints should be treated as reading experiments, not replacements for the earlier general-English checkpoints. No timing advantage is claimed because verification/evaluation ran concurrently with parts of training.

## Memory diagnostic

A controlled, equal-length substitution changed an earlier hat color between green and white while keeping the question fixed. Neutral filler increased the distance to the answer. For graph MLM, relative final-state difference fell from about 0.00262 with no filler to 0.0000458 with 34 filler bytes and about 0.00000020 with 136 bytes. Answer preference changed by only about 0.0000049 nats/byte initially and was near numerical noise with more filler. The GRU also lost sensitivity rapidly.

This is a diagnostic observation from one construction. It suggests a retention/readout problem worth isolating; it does not establish the sole cause of reading failure. Optimization, task design, finite training budget, and architectural capacity remain possible contributors. The raw measurements and in-domain subset scores are saved in memory-diagnostic.json.

## Reproduce

```sh
uv run python -m mlm.supervised_data --source data/hf --out data/assistant-v2
uv run mlm stream-train --train data/assistant-v2/train.jsonl --validation data/assistant-v2/validation.jsonl --test data/assistant-v2/test.jsonl --config configs/assistant-graph.json --init runs/english-v1/best.mlm --out runs/assistant-graph-new --steps 2000 --eval-every 500
uv run mlm stream-train --train data/assistant-v2/train.jsonl --validation data/assistant-v2/validation.jsonl --test data/assistant-v2/test.jsonl --config configs/assistant-gru.json --init runs/baseline-gru/best.mlm --out runs/assistant-gru-new --steps 2000 --eval-every 500
uv run python -m mlm.supervised_eval runs/assistant-graph-new/best.mlm --out results/assistant-graph-new-evaluation.json
```

Use fresh output directories. Prepared data is reused rather than silently overwritten. Public background data attribution and license links are in [data/README](../../data/README.md). Raw configs, environment/source fingerprints, metrics, masks/protocol identities, and checkpoints are preserved.

## Decision

Do not infer understanding from the lower answer loss. The immediate next research target is controlled delayed recall and a memory-timescale experiment, with fact sensitivity and English retention as explicit criteria. Compare that change against the unchanged graph and GRU before adding routing, rewiring, or growth. Assistant-only infrastructure is ready; reliable reading and general chat remain unachieved.

results/balanced-confirmation/report.md.text:
# Balanced confirmation with explicit English rehearsal

This experiment addresses the previous role-imbalanced split and increases training-name diversity while keeping the original sum-readout graph unchanged. It is a new snapshot and does not replace historical tests or outcomes.

## Dataset and balance

A fixed seed samples 64 artificial three-letter labels: 32 training, 16 new development and 16 new test names. Offline role classes are random strata and never appear in model prompts. Training uses 64 entity pairs: two within-role cycles and two cross-role matchings. Every training name has exactly four partners. Half of the training pairs are within-role and half cross-role; known held-out development/test pair identities are excluded.

Each training pair receives two disjoint color pairs covering all four colors, both color assignments, both queries and both sentence orders. There are 256 four-question groups / 1,024 training documents. Every document fits the 128-byte unroll. Source words and one English sentence grammar are shared across splits; names are held out within this binding task, not guaranteed globally new in English pretraining.

Development and test each contain 1,152 questions. The familiar-name bucket uses 16 disjoint pairs covering all 32 training names, half within-role and half cross-role, evaluated over all six color pairs and both fact orders: 96 eight-condition cases. The new-name bucket uses eight pairs covering all 16 split-specific names, also half within-role and half cross-role: 48 eight-condition cases. New-name pools, familiar pair identities and exact texts are disjoint where required. Unit tests verify these properties, partner degree, labels, spans, eight-condition completeness, and truncation bounds.

## Source, objectives and cost

Both arms start from `runs/english-v1/best.mlm`, the preserved 4,000-update English checkpoint, with a fresh optimizer. This differs from the previous memorization source: the current question is whether a clean English model can acquire binding while retaining English. Differences from earlier experiments cannot be attributed to balancing alone.

Both use seed 42, learning rate 0.001, batch four, unroll 128 and the same 2,000 complete-group QA updates in the same sampler order. QA loss supervises assistant color/newline and EOS; facts and question still update recurrent state. Task-only receives 2,000 optimizer updates. Rehearsal performs one full-document English training-stream chunk after each QA update, receiving 4,000 optimizer updates total. Rehearsal uses the cached 1,000 training stories, not development/test stories. QA state resets per example; English has its own persistent stream carry with truncated backpropagation. Adam state is shared within the rehearsal arm across both objectives.

Each batch loss is mean target cross-entropy. Alternating steps do not imply equal token counts or gradient contribution. Actual input/supervised-byte and update counts are recorded separately. QA exposure is matched; total compute, optimizer steps and input exposure are not. Checkpoints in the rehearsal arm are evaluated at the end of a full QA+English cycle. No speed, compute-efficiency or architecture-superiority claim follows from this comparison.

## Selection and test policy

Initial state and every 500 QA updates are eligible. Primary binding score is the macro-average complete eight-condition correctness of the familiar-name and new-name development buckets; their different sizes do not give the larger bucket extra weight. Both sentence orders, both assignments and both queried people must be correct. QA development loss breaks ties; exact ties preserve earlier weights.

Two policies are saved per arm:

- `best-task.mlm`: strongest development binding score, unconstrained by English.
- `best.mlm`: strongest binding score among checkpoints whose English development loss is at most 1.25 times the initial source loss. Step zero is eligible, so this may be a source fallback rather than a newly learned model.

English development is explicitly a selection constraint. English test remains unopened until all four selected checkpoints are locked, and is a reused retention diagnostic rather than fresh independent generalization evidence. Task test is newly generated and never chooses a checkpoint or hyperparameter. The budget, source, data, config and runner hashes are frozen in protocol.json. There is no sweep or resume feature. The runner rejects nonempty output paths.

Primary task results use two-choice frozen neural likelihood ranking. Raw greedy answers are preserved separately for fixed samples and must not be confused with full-test ranking. Offline labels, role tags and grouping only construct/grade data; no inference answer lookup or regex solver is added. Names are synthetic and grammar is shared, so success would not establish broad conversation or natural-language comprehension. One seed does not establish a robust general advantage.

## Reproduction

Use fresh paths and preserve source/cache files.

```sh
uv run python -m mlm.confirmation_data --out data/confirmation-new
uv run python -m mlm.confirmation_run --data data/confirmation-new --config configs/confirmation-graph.json --init runs/english-v1/best.mlm --out runs/confirmation-task-new --steps 2000 --eval-every 500
uv run python -m mlm.confirmation_run --data data/confirmation-new --config configs/confirmation-graph.json --init runs/english-v1/best.mlm --out runs/confirmation-rehearsal-new --steps 2000 --eval-every 500 --rehearsal
uv run python -m mlm.gradual_eval runs/confirmation-rehearsal-new/best.mlm --questions data/confirmation-new/test-questions.json --out results/confirmation-rehearsal-new.json
```

Run the last command only after locking both policies from both completed arms. Repeat for unconstrained best-task checkpoints and the source reference as separately labelled results. The original graph topology, parameter/state budget, and inference algorithm are unchanged.

## Verified selection and exposure

Both arms completed all 2,000 QA updates. QA sampler order, cursor, RNG and group identities match exactly, and both consume 776,000 QA input bytes and 40,000 supervised QA payload bytes. The rehearsal arm additionally performs 2,000 English updates, consuming and supervising 958,088 English payload bytes. Thus total optimizer calls are 2,000 versus 4,000, and input exposure is 776,000 versus 1,734,088 bytes. Rehearsal's added resource cost is explicit; these results do not establish a cheaper training method.

The initial English development loss is 1.155704; the predeclared constraint is 1.444630. Task-only development loss rises above this limit at every trained checkpoint. Its protected selection is therefore QA step zero, with parameter hash verified identical to the original English source; this is a fallback, not a successful new binding model. Its unconstrained task selection is QA step 1,500. Rehearsal selects QA step 2,000 / optimizer step 4,000 under both policies. Those two slots have identical parameter hashes and are the same trained model, not independent successes.

All development eight-condition binding scores remain zero, so QA loss is the tiebreaker. Rehearsal's lower QA loss is therefore not evidence of semantic success. Protected selection enforces only an English prediction constraint; it does not guarantee successful adaptation. All four selected checkpoint hashes and source identities were locked before task or English test scoring.

## Test results

| Arm / policy | Selected QA / optimizer updates | Familiar-name cases correct /96 | New-name cases correct /48 | English test loss |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Task-only, protected source fallback | 0 / 0 | 0 | 0 | 1.121557 |
| Task-only, unconstrained | 1,500 / 1,500 | 0 | 0 | 3.381755 |
| Rehearsal, protected and unconstrained (same model) | 2,000 / 4,000 | 0 | 0 | 1.087839 |

A case requires all eight color-assignment/query/sentence-order conditions correct. All within-role and cross-role strata also score zero complete cases. Individual candidate-ranking accuracy is exactly 50% and preferred answers do not change with context/query swaps for these selected models. This is consistent with fixed answer preferences, not useful binding. Full item scores and histograms are preserved; the larger balanced test does not demonstrate name-independent retrieval under this acquisition protocol.

Rehearsal preserves and slightly improves held-out English byte prediction relative to the source, while unconstrained task-only adaptation harms it substantially. English test is a repeatedly inspected retention diagnostic, so this is one measured run rather than independent broad generalization evidence. The preserved English source remains available. The rehearsal model is a retention-compatible research candidate; it is not a capable chatbot or an accepted binding upgrade.

The protected task-only selection doubles as the source reference on this fresh task. The duplicate rehearsal policy result is explicitly labelled as equivalent checkpoint reuse; only three unique parameter sets were evaluated. Eight raw greedy samples per unique checkpoint (first full group per bucket) are saved separately. Those samples are not a full-test generation benchmark, and no answer extraction/repair is applied.

## Interpretation

The balanced benchmark removes the previously discovered within/cross-role split imbalance and increases the training pool from eight to 32 names. It does not by itself resolve binding learning. Compared with the earlier partial-transfer study, source weights, learning rate, name count, task size and training schedule also changed. This is a new acquisition-and-retention setting, not a source-matched replication proving that all earlier transfer was invalid or that balancing alone caused failure.

The original English model can learn short answer formatting and maintain English with explicit replay, but no reusable entity–fact retrieval rule was demonstrated within this budget. This does not establish an architecture impossibility: insufficient task progression, optimization, memory initialization and data exposure remain possible contributors. Further diagnosis should hold source/learning rate fixed while scaling a balanced task from small memorized cases to more names, and distinguish failure to fit training from failure to transfer. More architecture or capacity is not yet supported as a proven remedy.

No graph growth, rewiring, learned edges, online inference-time weight updates, or new readout was introduced. Parameters remain 366,722 with the original recurrent state budget. Inference stays entirely neural. Offline labels, matching/cycle construction and role strata are dataset/evaluation logic, never an answer solver.

## Verification and decision

All 50 regression tests pass. Ruff lint/format and source type checks pass. Tests cover balanced partitions, partner degree, exact-text/name/pair disjointness, labels/spans and eight-condition completeness, objective counters, protected selection, output protection and source immutability, alongside prior model/state/checkpoint tests. Dataset/config/source/code hashes and matched QA exposure were verified before final scoring.

Keep all checkpoints and negative results as research evidence. Do not promote a binding-capability claim from low answer loss or English retention alone. The next focused study needs a source-controlled balanced learning ladder, with retention evaluated explicitly and a fresh independent confirmation set after tuning.

# Balanced binding confirmation and explicit English rehearsal

Authorized next research step: fix the discovered pair-role imbalance, increase name diversity, keep the sum-readout graph unchanged, and explicitly test retention. This is a fresh experiment, not a silent replacement of the previous test.

Generate 64 deterministic three-letter pronounceable entity labels: 32 training, 16 new development, 16 new test. Role A/B classes are random offline strata, never model inputs. Training uses 64 entity pairs from two within-role cycles and two cross-role matchings, excluding held-out familiar-name development/test pairs. All training names have four partners; 32 pairs are within-role and 32 cross-role. Each pair gets two disjoint color pairs covering all four colors and both sentence orders. Training has 256 four-question groups / 1,024 documents. Each familiar-name evaluation pool uses 16 disjoint pairs covering all 32 training names, half within-role and half cross-role. New-name pools use eight pairs covering all 16 new names, also balanced. All six color pairs and both sentence orders are evaluated. Development/test pairs and exact text are disjoint; new-name pools are disjoint. Names are not guaranteed globally unseen in English pretraining.

Use runs/english-v1/best.mlm (original English graph) as the common source, fresh optimizer, seed 42, LR 0.001, batch four, unroll 128. Source is intentionally different from the prior memorization source: this study asks whether a clean English model can acquire binding while retaining its English. Comparisons with prior runs cannot isolate dataset balancing alone.

Both arms receive the same 2,000 complete-group QA updates in the same sampler order. Task-only gets those 2,000 optimizer updates. Rehearsal interleaves one full-document English training-stream chunk after each QA update, for 4,000 optimizer updates total. Adam state is shared across the two objectives in the rehearsal arm; recurrent state is separate, with independent QA resets and English stream carry detached across chunks. This matches task exposure, not total compute, input bytes, or update count. Both losses are mean target cross-entropy per batch; alternating steps are not a guarantee of equal gradient contribution. No story targets are secretly mixed into QA documents.

Evaluate at initial state and every 500 QA updates. Primary binding measure: macro-average of complete eight-condition correctness across familiar-name and new-name development buckets, each including both fact orders; target QA loss breaks ties. Save best-task.mlm without an English constraint. Save best.mlm only when English development loss <=1.25 times the initial English development loss, using the same binding/loss ordering. Initial state is eligible and provides the protected fallback. English TEST is not opened until checkpoint locks; development is used for the retention constraint. Report selected steps, task and total optimizer counts, actual per-objective bytes/chunks, and source identity. No resume support claimed; refuse nonempty output directories.

Freeze data/config/source/code hashes before training and lock all selected checkpoints before testing. Report protected and unconstrained checkpoints separately, identify step-zero fallbacks explicitly, and score familiar/new-name and within/cross strata. Use untouched new task test samples and the reused English test as a retention diagnostic. Record raw greedy samples separately from neural candidate ranking. One seed, artificial names, four colors and shared grammar do not establish broad language understanding. No hyperparameter sweep or architecture change.

Tests cover balanced partition counts, degree/partner coverage, pair/text/name disjointness, all eight conditions and unroll/mask bounds, protected selection, source preservation, objective counters and fresh-output guard. Implement confirmation_data.py and confirmation_run.py using existing neural training/scoring utilities. Save results and update research/PRD/README with actual outcomes and limitations.

# Equal-exposure acquisition control

Both modes independently trained the same 16-group subset from their own frozen English checkpoint for 2,000 updates. This gives exactly 125 complete-group presentations per group, matching the successful four-group/500-update trials. The old 16-group trials received only 31–32 presentations per group in 500 updates. Learning rate 0.003, seed 42, batch 4/unroll 128, architecture, routing auxiliary and task-only schedule remain unchanged. There is no English rehearsal, curriculum or split-rate update in this study. No test data was opened and no checkpoint was selected by development score: all results describe fixed endpoints.

## Results

| Model | Groups | Updates | Presentations/group | Training answers correct | Complete training groups | Familiar-pool dev cases | New-pool dev cases | English dev loss |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| dense | 4 | 500 | 125 | 16/16 | 4/4 | 0/96 | 0/48 | 5.586892 |
| dense | 16 | 500 | 31–32 | 32/64 | 0/16 | 0/96 | 0/48 | 5.210094 |
| dense | 16 | 2000 | 125 | 33/64 | 0/16 | 0/96 | 0/48 | 9.424430 |
| hierarchical | 4 | 500 | 125 | 16/16 | 4/4 | 0/96 | 0/48 | 6.798242 |
| hierarchical | 16 | 500 | 31–32 | 36/64 | 1/16 | 0/96 | 0/48 | 4.981437 |
| hierarchical | 16 | 2000 | 125 | 61/64 | 14/16 | 0/96 | 0/48 | 9.336111 |

Answer accuracy ranks two candidate colors by neural likelihood. A training group requires all four fact-assignment/query conditions; a development case requires all eight including both fact orders. These definitions differ deliberately and are not interchangeable. Source English development losses are 1.155704 dense and 1.352696 hierarchical. All task-only checkpoints remain diagnostics; no English/chat model is promoted.

## What the extra exposure changes

dense: training answer accuracy 50.00% → 51.56%; complete training groups 0/16 → 0/16. English development loss 5.210094 → 9.424430.

hierarchical: training answer accuracy 56.25% → 95.31%; complete training groups 1/16 → 14/16. English development loss 4.981437 → 9.336111.


This is an exposure control, not a compute-matched comparison: the new 16-group endpoint costs four times as many updates as either archived 500-update endpoint. Larger subsets also contain more names, pairs and color combinations. Matching repetitions does not remove task-diversity or optimization effects. Architectures use their own independently pretrained sources, so this compares complete pipelines rather than changing routing on one identical learned tensor set. One seed, narrow grammar, four color words and reused exploratory development data limit inference. Only initial and final states are scored; intermediate success or late instability cannot be ruled out. Better training fit demonstrates acquisition for these examples, not a general binding algorithm; failure at one finite endpoint cannot prove a capacity limit.

## Name coverage

The 16-group subset contains 26 of the full 32 task-training names. The old familiar-name development category is defined relative to that full pool; its names are not all present in this smaller trial. Below, each case is stratified by how many of its two entity names actually appeared in these training groups. Pair identities are disjoint from development. Absence from task training does not imply absence from English pretraining.

| Model | Zero seen names | One seen name | Two seen names |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| dense | 0/60 | 0/12 | 0/72 |
| hierarchical | 0/60 | 0/12 | 0/72 |

Counts combine the two development categories and require all eight conditions. They avoid labeling names familiar merely because they belong to the full source task pool.

## Integrity and reproducibility

The paired update traces, source fingerprints, subset IDs and byte counters are checked in summary.json. Each group appears exactly 125 times. The first 500 sampled group IDs exactly match the archived 16-group trial; the initial parameter fingerprint and fresh optimizer also match. The original source/config/data/code/baseline hashes remain unchanged. Original weights are preserved. Fixed initial/final scores and raw generations are archived; correct answers/fact metadata grade predictions offline and are not an inference solver. Scheduler rules and experimental checks do not replace the neural answer computation.

```sh
uv run python -m mlm.acquisition_run --config configs/acquisition-dense.json --init runs/scratch-english-dense-v1/best.mlm --out runs/exposure-dense-new --sizes 16 --steps 2000
uv run python -m mlm.acquisition_run --config configs/acquisition-hierarchical.json --init runs/scratch-english-hierarchical-v1/best.mlm --out runs/exposure-hierarchical-new --sizes 16 --steps 2000
```

The unchanged fresh-only runner and existing regression tests are reused; no model or training implementation changed. Final checkpoints remain in runs/exposure-{mode}-v1/groups-16/final.mlm. Source/tests/config/lockfile snapshots and their SHA256 hashes accompany this report. protocol.json records the pre-run frozen inputs. execution-status.json records completed checks separately from the frozen plan.

## Next decision

The next isolated experiment is a shared-versus-node learning-rate control with explicit uniform-rate and English-rehearsal baselines. It should compare acquisition and retention under declared budgets, with router rates specified separately. Do not stack growth, deeper processing and adaptive curricula into the same change. No claim of Transformer replacement or general chat competence follows from these trials. Fresh confirmation data is required after choosing training changes from these exploratory results.

# QA ordering versus English replay sampling

In this selected, fixed-initialization comparison, acquisition follows the English replay stream. Both QA orderings learn16/16 training rankings and4/4 groups with English seed43. With English seed44, they learn7/16 and8/16, with0/4 complete groups. The new crossed runs narrow the earlier combined-schedule finding to English replay sampling for these tested levels.

This does not identify a general mechanism or establish reliable generalization. English seed changes document exposure/order and byte budget together. Two cells are historical, levels were outcome-selected, and the sampler-control driver has a reviewed, compatibility-tested source change. All cells still complete zero tiny development groups; the earlier independent adaptation-seed replication gate remains failed.

## Results

Memory initialization is fixed to the saved step-zero initializer42 throughout. All non-memory source tensors and every memory tensor match across initial states.

| QA seed | English seed | Provenance | Training rankings | Complete training groups | Fixed raw training samples | English dev loss |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 42 | 43 | reused historical | 16/16 | 4/4 | 4/4 | 1.286896 |
| 42 | 44 | new crossed run | 7/16 | 0/4 | 2/4 | 1.265234 |
| 43 | 43 | new crossed run | 16/16 | 4/4 | 4/4 | 1.287316 |
| 43 | 44 | reused historical | 8/16 | 0/4 | 2/4 | 1.270391 |

Every cell scores4/8 questions,0/2 complete groups and0/1 complete eight-condition case on the reused tiny development set. All pass the predefined retention threshold1.6908700424 (1.25×source loss1.3526960339). The English44 cells have lower English loss while failing binding acquisition; lower language loss alone does not establish the intended binding behavior.

Raw samples are the fixed first four training prompts, greedy max12 bytes, graded only by strip/casefold. E43 yields4/4 raw answers and E44 yields2/4. Candidate rankings cover all16 questions; raw generation does not. No parser, extraction, label-driven routing or answer repair was added.

Each new trial receives2,000QA+2,000English updates,4000 optimizer steps,500 presentations per group. New trial work totals8000 updates. The separate old/new-default compatibility preflight uses32 optimizer updates total. No budget extension, replacement cell, best-checkpoint selection, new test data, trained ablation or model promotion occurred.

## What changed in the runner

`mlm.plasticity_run` now accepts `--qa-seed` and `--english-seed`. QA seed changes only complete-group ordering; English seed changes only `DocumentStream` sampling. Config.seed still controls initialization and subset selection. Omitted overrides preserve QA=config.seed and English=config.seed+1. Explicit zero is supported; invalid seeds fail before output creation. Old programmatic Namespaces without the new fields continue to work. The resolved subset/QA/English policy is saved in protocol, summary and checkpoint metadata.

Both new runs use config.seed42 and the same complete four-group pool, with QA42/English44 and QA43/English43. The historical QA43/English44 cell used config.seed43, but its memory initialization is also42 and all four groups were selected. Full tensor identity, membership, natural batch order/actual QA trace and stream audits establish the intended separation. No Config schema, topology, model, gradient, optimizer, loss, scorer or data-generation code changed.

The only source/test changes are the reviewed runner and its test. Their old versions are preserved under `legacy/`. Dynamic invalid-config test construction also uses Pydantic's model_validate API to avoid a type-check ambiguity; validation semantics are preserved. A reconstructed legacy source digest, substituting the archived driver into otherwise unchanged model sources, exactly matches both historical digests.

## Descriptive contrasts and limits

For complete-group fraction, English44 minus43 is−1.0 at each QA seed:−100 percentage points. The averaged QA43-minus42 contrast and interaction are0. For question accuracy, English44-minus43 averages−0.53125 (−53.125pp), QA43-minus42 averages+0.03125 (+3.125pp), and interaction is+0.0625 (+6.25pp). These are descriptive differences over the selected table, not statistical population effects.

Replay43 consumes958,088 English bytes and replay44 consumes958,288 bytes per run; each cell consumes776,000 QA input bytes with40,000 supervised QA targets. Replay changes document content/position/exposure as well as order and has a200-byte total difference. The study cannot separate these components, attribute failure to particular stories, or prove gradient interference. Objective interference and replay-content sensitivity remain hypotheses, not measured mechanisms.

There is one run per cell and one memory initializer. Two reference cells were already observed; no fresh four-cell replication or new graph-architecture comparison occurred. Defaults were checked on a bounded preflight, not by retraining the historical4000-step endpoints. Recorded Python/dependency/platform/backend fields match, and the known historical QA43/English44 numerical flags match current settings. QA42/English43 historical numerical/thread flags were not recorded, so full historical/current numerical equivalence cannot be proven. The implementation-version and historical reuse limitations remain explicit.

## Verification

The new QA-override test first failed on the actual wrong sampler trace before implementation. All9 targeted plasticity tests then passed in59.02s, followed by the complete suite:75 tests in234.90s. Coverage includes independently overridden QA and English streams, actual English input batches, zero seeds, legacy Namespace/default behavior, source preservation, fresh optimizer, continued English carry and exact default-versus-explicit legacy parameter/moment equality. Invalid seeds are tested.

The actual preserved old driver and updated default path also match bitwise for all parameters/Adam moments, metrics, QA trace, counters, English stream/carry and initial fingerprints after eight QA/rehearsal pairs. All13 compatibility checks pass. The environment/source preflight passes9 checks and identifies exactly the two intentional changed files. Ruff lint/format and ty checks passed. Independent review approved implementation, audit logic, frozen cell mappings and all115 input hashes before launch.

Both new processes completed normally. All219 input/endpoint audit checks pass: fixed initializer tensors, fresh optimizer, actual final steps/config/counters/finite parameters, exactly500/group, QA trace and byte counts against the same-QA reference, English snapshot/bytes against the same-English reference, actual seed policies in all metadata, frozen child numerical/environment settings, full train/dev question evidence, score-derived argmax/correctness/metrics and fixed raw prompts.

See [protocol](protocol.json), [summary](summary.json), [audit](audit.json), [compatibility evidence](compatibility.json), [source/environment audit](environment-preflight.json) and logs. Measure whether English replay updates oppose QA learning on predefined training batches and frozen checkpoints. Report objective-gradient alignment and the actual QA-loss change from a copied English optimizer step; a gradient cosine alone does not capture Adam's moments, clipping and per-role scaling. This would test a possible mechanism without changing model weights on disk or opening test data. Then select one controlled training intervention if supported, with fixed English exposure/budgets and acquisition/retention gates. Do not hardcode a favorable replay seed as a solution or claim general understanding from this tiny fit.
