# Shared/node learning rates and English rehearsal

Six fresh trials test three learning-rate policies with and without English rehearsal. Every trial starts from the same hierarchical model's frozen English checkpoint, with fresh optimizer state, the same 16 complete training groups, seed 42, batch 4/unroll 128 and 2,000 QA updates. Each group receives exactly 125 presentations. Rehearsal adds 2,000 full-document English updates, with separate streaming carry and accounting. Endpoints are fixed; no test files are opened and no checkpoint is selected by scores.

The architecture is unchanged: fixed eight-node graph, width 64, hierarchical soft updates and sum readout. This is an optimizer/data-schedule experiment, not growth, sparse dispatch or an adaptive learning-rate controller.

## Rate policies

| Policy | Shared representation rate | Node-specific rate | Router rate |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| high | 0.003 | 0.003 | 0.003 |
| low | 0.0003 | 0.0003 | 0.0003 |
| split | 0.0003 | 0.003 | 0.003 |

Node parameters are input_kernel, hidden_kernel, gru_bias and read_kernel. Shared representations comprise embedding, message_kernel, normalization and vocabulary head. Group/child router kernels and biases have their own explicit role; they stay fast in the split arm. This does not test a slower-router alternative. The role registry rejects unknown parameters when applying non-default scales. Completed AdamW updates are scaled after global clipping and moment estimation; decoupled decay follows the effective learning rate. Defaults remain identical to the old optimizer, including state structure. Scale settings are serialized in Config and restored by checkpoint loading.

## Measured outcomes

Training answers are two-candidate neural likelihood rankings. A complete training group requires four assignment/query conditions; development requires eight including both fact orders. Source English development loss is 1.352696. The predeclared diagnostic gate requires at least 14/16 complete training groups and English development loss ≤1.25× source. It tests acquisition plus retention only and neither selects nor promotes a model.

| Arm | Optimizer updates | Train answers correct | Complete train groups | Familiar-pool dev cases | New-pool dev cases | English dev loss | Source multiple | Joint diagnostic gate |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| high-task | 2000 | 61/64 | 14/16 | 0/96 | 0/48 | 9.336111 | 6.902× | fails |
| high-rehearsal | 4000 | 64/64 | 16/16 | 0/96 | 0/48 | 1.319806 | 0.976× | meets |
| low-task | 2000 | 56/64 | 12/16 | 0/96 | 0/48 | 3.537662 | 2.615× | fails |
| low-rehearsal | 4000 | 45/64 | 5/16 | 0/96 | 0/48 | 1.307681 | 0.967× | fails |
| split-task | 2000 | 64/64 | 16/16 | 0/96 | 0/48 | 6.268202 | 4.634× | fails |
| split-rehearsal | 4000 | 64/64 | 16/16 | 0/96 | 0/48 | 1.305334 | 0.965× | meets |

## Controlled contrasts

high: adding rehearsal changes complete training groups 14/16 → 16/16, and English development loss 9.336111 → 1.319806. Rehearsal adds 2,000 optimizer updates.

low: adding rehearsal changes complete training groups 12/16 → 5/16, and English development loss 3.537662 → 1.307681. Rehearsal adds 2,000 optimizer updates.

split: adding rehearsal changes complete training groups 16/16 → 16/16, and English development loss 6.268202 → 1.305334. Rehearsal adds 2,000 optimizer updates.

Within task, split versus low uniform changes complete training groups 12/16 → 16/16 and English loss 3.537662 → 6.268202. Shared representation rates match, but both node and router rates are 10× higher in split.

Within rehearsal, split versus low uniform changes complete training groups 5/16 → 16/16 and English loss 1.307681 → 1.305334. Shared representation rates match, but both node and router rates are 10× higher in split.


The high-versus-split comparison changes only the shared representation rate within each schedule. Low uniform controls for slowing the whole network. Rehearsal versus task-only is QA-exposure matched but not compute matched: it doubles optimizer updates. No causal claim that a particular tensor stores English follows from parameter drift or this one-seed study.

## Coverage, costs and evidence

The subset contains 26 of 32 task-training names. Familiar-name development is defined relative to the full 32-name pool. Name-coverage artifacts separately count cases with zero, one or two names present in this actual subset; no development pair is a training pair. Labels may have occurred in English pretraining. Both development categories remain narrow shared-grammar diagnostics, not independent final confirmation.

| Arm | QA payload bytes | QA supervised bytes | English payload/supervised bytes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| high-task | 776,000 | 40,000 | 0 |
| high-rehearsal | 776,000 | 40,000 | 958,088 |
| low-task | 776,000 | 40,000 | 0 |
| low-rehearsal | 776,000 | 40,000 | 958,088 |
| split-task | 776,000 | 40,000 | 0 |
| split-rehearsal | 776,000 | 40,000 | 958,088 |

All QA traces, initial parameters and QA byte counters match. Rehearsal arms also match English sampler snapshots and byte counters. The high/task endpoint exactly reproduces the earlier equal-exposure model's parameters and full optimizer state, auditing that defaults and the new runner preserved the original training behavior. Source/code/config/data/baseline hashes remain frozen. Full initial/final scored items, fixed first-group raw samples without answer repair, optimizer policies, checkpoints, stream state and parameter-change norms are saved. Grading labels never enter the neural scorer as expected answers.

The full regression suite and separate code review validate the implementation, including completed-update scaling, populated optimizer resets, carried English state, exact QA sampling, legacy checkpoints without new fields, and split-rate checkpoint continuation. Source/test/config/lock snapshots have hashes. Only initial/final scores are evaluated; intermediate acquisition or instability cannot be ruled out. All arms deliberately reset Adam moments; this is adaptation from pretrained weights, not uninterrupted continual training. A warm-optimizer control would be required before generalizing to continuous training. One seed, a small synthetic subset and reused development sets limit generalization.

## Next gate

Arms meeting the predeclared acquisition/retention diagnostic: high-rehearsal, split-rehearsal. No arm solves a complete development binding case. No endpoint is promoted. Any next curriculum or replay adjustment must retain matched controls and an explicit compute budget. If joint acquisition/retention improves, the remaining gate is transfer to unseen pairings, names and wording, evaluated on fresh confirmation after development choices. Otherwise diagnose optimization and interference before adding capacity. These outcomes do not establish Transformer replacement, dynamic growth, sparse speedups or arbitrary-device deployment.

## Reproduction

```sh
uv run python -m mlm.plasticity_run --config configs/plasticity-split.json --init runs/scratch-english-hierarchical-v1/best.mlm --out runs/plasticity-split-new --groups 16 --steps 2000 --rehearsal
```

Use high/low configs and omit --rehearsal for task-only arms; every output path must be fresh. The driver has no resume feature, but standard checkpoint loading restores its rate settings and Adam state. Stream resume rejects the experimental checkpoint mode. Commands for all six arms and frozen hashes are in protocol.json. Weights remain under runs/plasticity-{arm}-v1/final.mlm. Historical models and previous result snapshots are preserved.

Verification: all 63 regression tests passed in 161.72 seconds; the five strengthened split-rate tests passed separately. Ruff lint/format and source type checks passed after archiving. The code review has no unresolved findings. See verification.json.

results/retrieval-curriculum/report.md.text:
# Controlled entity–fact retrieval curriculum

This experiment isolates a language model's ability to retrieve the color assigned to a queried person. It uses synthetic English sentences with the same grammar across splits. It does not test broad chat or transfer to unfamiliar wording. The graph and GRU architectures, learned update equations, parameter counts, and state sizes remain unchanged.

## Design

The offline generator writes sentences such as `Ada's color is blue. Ben's color is pink.` and asks `What color belongs to Ada?`. All four answer colors have four ASCII bytes: blue, gold, lime, pink. There are 16 training names, eight development names, and eight test names, disjoint within this task. They are not guaranteed unseen in earlier English training or earlier experiments.

There are nine difficulty cells: zero, one, or three distractors, crossed with 0, 64, or 128 bytes of neutral filler. Each document assigns a unique color to each person. A context-swap pair exchanges the queried person's color and an alternative, keeping the question and candidate choices fixed. Binding cells additionally ask about the other person with exactly the same context, producing four-question groups. Correctness on the whole group requires both context swaps and query swaps to be answered correctly. The generator balances query position by reversing fact order, and records the factual assignments for offline validation only.

Two-choice candidate ranking uses the frozen neural model's answer-byte log probabilities. Labels and factual metadata grade predictions; they never enter neural scoring. Candidates are not inserted into the prompt. Raw greedy decoding is also saved for the first complete group from each cell, selected without inspecting outputs. It uses whitespace/case normalization only, with no answer extraction or repair. Two-choice ranking and unrestricted generation are different measures.

Independent fair two-choice guesses average 50% individual accuracy, 25% complete context pairs, and 6.25% complete four-question groups. A fixed answer can achieve 50% individual accuracy while solving no complete pairs. A first/last-fact preference can respond to a context swap without correctly using the query. These reference rates are not significance tests, and examples within a group are dependent.

## Training and selection

Both models start from their respective English-derived retention-bias initializations. No weights selected using previous reading-test results are used. Each receives a basic single-fact/no-delay stage of 500 updates, then a binding/delay stage of 1,500 updates initialized from the basic development-selected checkpoint. Each stage creates a fresh optimizer. Basic validation occurs every 250 updates; binding validation every 500. Minimum stage-specific development target loss selects checkpoints, including step zero.

Both use seed 42, batch size four, unroll 384, and learning rate 0.0005. Every synthetic example is at most 268 input bytes including BOS and fits in one unroll, so its answer loss can backpropagate to all of its facts. The binding training set includes 32 cached public training stories with explicit full-text loss as rehearsal. The synthetic records supervise only assistant answer/newline and EOS; prompt bytes still update neural state.

The basic training set has 64 documents; the full training set has 960 synthetic documents plus 32 stories. Development and test each contain 480 synthetic documents spanning all cells; their basic subsets each contain 32. Synthetic example selection, names, data files, configurations, and source checkpoint hashes are frozen in protocol.json. Final selected checkpoint hashes are recorded before opening test questions. This is one seed and a bounded synthetic task; positive findings require further independent confirmation.

## Reproduction

Reuse the existing public cache and English-derived retention initializations. Choose fresh output paths.

```sh
uv run python -m mlm.retrieval_data --out data/retrieval-new --source data/hf
uv run mlm stream-train --train data/retrieval-new/basic-train.jsonl --validation data/retrieval-new/basic-validation.jsonl --config configs/retrieval-graph.json --init runs/memory-init-graph/initial.mlm --out runs/retrieval-basic-graph-new --steps 500 --eval-every 250
uv run mlm stream-train --train data/retrieval-new/train.jsonl --validation data/retrieval-new/validation.jsonl --config configs/retrieval-graph.json --init runs/retrieval-basic-graph-new/best.mlm --out runs/retrieval-binding-graph-new --steps 1500 --eval-every 500
uv run python -m mlm.retrieval_eval runs/retrieval-binding-graph-new/best.mlm --questions data/retrieval-new/test-questions.json --out results/retrieval-graph-new.json
uv run mlm evaluate runs/retrieval-binding-graph-new/best.mlm --data data/hf/stories/test.jsonl --full-documents
```

For the GRU substitute configs/retrieval-gru.json, runs/memory-init-gru/initial.mlm, and fresh GRU output paths. Run and lock both models before examining test outcomes. Repeated tuning against these test questions would make them development data.

## Results

Both basic stages completed 500 updates and selected step 500. Both binding stages completed 1,500 updates and selected step 1,500. The selection lock was written and checkpoint/data hashes verified before retrieval test evaluation. Training/development identities, supervision masks, final sampler snapshots, input exposure, and supervised-byte exposure matched between architectures in each stage. The basic stage consumed 152,000 payload bytes and supervised 10,000; the binding stage consumed 1,091,028 and supervised 152,091.

Both basic-stage checkpoints answered all 32 fresh single-fact/no-delay test questions correctly by candidate likelihood, including all 16 counterfactual pairs. This is successful narrow recall on held-out task names with shared grammar, not evidence of query binding: there is only one person's fact to choose from. Raw greedy examples are saved separately.

After binding adaptation, graph answers 281/480 individual test questions correctly (58.54%) and GRU 291/480 (60.63%). Complete context-pair accuracy is 68/240 for graph and 66/240 for GRU. **Neither solves any of the 96 complete four-question binding groups.** Only 6/192 fixed-context query pairs are both correct for graph, and 8/192 for GRU. Preferred answers change with the query in 19/192 and 13/192 cases respectively; many changes are wrong. Individual accuracy is not a reliable substitute for the binding measure.

| Difficulty cell | Graph individual | GRU individual | Graph complete binding groups | GRU complete binding groups |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| d0-delay0 | 100.0% | 100.0% | — | — |
| d0-delay128 | 100.0% | 100.0% | — | — |
| d0-delay64 | 100.0% | 100.0% | — | — |
| d1-delay0 | 50.0% | 50.0% | 0.0% | 0.0% |
| d1-delay128 | 46.9% | 50.0% | 0.0% | 0.0% |
| d1-delay64 | 45.3% | 50.0% | 0.0% | 0.0% |
| d3-delay0 | 51.6% | 46.9% | 0.0% | 0.0% |
| d3-delay128 | 50.0% | 53.1% | 0.0% | 0.0% |
| d3-delay64 | 45.3% | 54.7% | 0.0% | 0.0% |

Each single-fact cell contains 32 questions / 16 context pairs. Each binding cell contains 64 questions / 32 context pairs / 16 four-question groups. The gap between single-fact and multiple-fact performance is the important diagnostic; aggregate accuracy blends them. All group failures are preserved, including contradictory query/context preferences.

Graph: across all delays, single-fact individual accuracy is 100.00%; multiple-fact individual accuracy is 48.18%. The fixed 30-example raw greedy sample scores 50.00%. Greedy outputs are unedited and this small sample is not a full-test generation score.

Gru: across all delays, single-fact individual accuracy is 100.00%; multiple-fact individual accuracy is 50.78%. The fixed 30-example raw greedy sample scores 50.00%. Greedy outputs are unedited and this small sample is not a full-test generation score.

## English retention and supervision exposure

Story test loss after the basic stage is 3.487491 for graph and 4.133074 for GRU. After the binding/rehearsal stage it is 1.577292 and 1.264509. Recovery coincides with story rehearsal but no no-rehearsal control was run, so rehearsal is not an isolated causal explanation. Both remain worse than their English source checkpoints (1.121557 and 1.098890). Preserve the original English checkpoints; these are task experiments, not accepted English/chat upgrades.

The 32 stories are only about 3.2% of training documents, but a deterministic stream replay verifies 124,221 of 152,091 supervised payload bytes come from stories, versus 27,870 from synthetic retrieval. Thus roughly 81.7% of scored payload bytes are rehearsal. Per-update masking and normalization mean this is not an exact fraction of gradient contribution. It shows why document-count ratios alone are insufficient. The exposure audit and matched-stream checks are saved with raw evidence.

Final held-out assistant-target loss is 0.147348 for graph and 0.146569 for GRU. These losses include answer spelling, newline, and EOS; they must not be presented as comprehension accuracy or compared directly with full-text story loss.

## Interpretation and next experiment

The current networks can learn single-fact recall with this grammar and new task names. They do not demonstrate reliable entity–fact binding under the tested curriculum, budget, and selection rule. Longer-lived state and a lower supervised loss are insufficient evidence of successful query-dependent retrieval. This does not prove that the architecture cannot learn binding: optimization, curriculum, data coverage, and supervision balance remain confounded.

The training data uses a bounded set of paired query entities, one shared sentence template, four colors, and one seed. Compared with earlier runs, data, curriculum, and unroll changed together. There is no unshifted-gate control on this new task, so these results cannot isolate a benefit of the retention intervention. Runtime contention also rules out a controlled speed comparison.

Before increasing graph size, isolate the smallest failed case: one distractor, zero filler, varied entity pairings, and an explicitly accounted task/rehearsal objective. Use complete fixed-context query swaps as the primary development metric, with target loss as a secondary measure. A query-conditioned node readout or associative memory is a subsequent architecture hypothesis, not an already-established cure. Any tuning after viewing these outcomes must use a new confirmation test set.

All 39 regression tests passed, and lint, formatting, and source type checks passed. New tests cover offline labels/spans, split identity, exact delays, unroll bounds, swaps, grouping, and aggregation that distinguishes wrong query flips from correct answers. Inference still consists only of learned neural computation. Dataset label generation and evaluation keys never serve as an answer solver; no regex or response lookup was added. Node growth and learned topology remain unimplemented.

English story scores reuse a previously inspected retention diagnostic; they are not fresh independent generalization evidence.

# Controlled entity–fact retrieval curriculum

Authorized next experiment: learn which fact belongs to the queried entity, with controlled distractors and delay. Keep fixed graph/GRU architecture and existing retention-bias initialization; no new inference rules or learned topology.

Alternatives considered: add a memory bank (larger architectural confound), train more on the old reading suite (continued test reuse), or isolate binding in a controlled curriculum (chosen). Fixed English grammar and equal-four-byte color answers isolate retrieval from new wording and answer-length effects. Entity names are disjoint across this task's splits, not necessarily unseen in English pretraining or earlier experiments.

Data: offline factual assignments, paired context swaps, and four-question binding groups that also swap queried entity with context fixed. Three distractor levels 0/1/3 and exact filler byte lengths 0/64/128. Facts assign distinct colors. Query positions are balanced. Report all difficulty cells, full groups, correct and incorrect answer flips, raw greedy outputs, and story retention. Random independent two-choice guesses average 50% individual, 25% complete pairs and 6.25% complete four-question groups; these are reference rates, not significance claims.

Curriculum: two separate stages with fresh optimizers. Basic single-fact/no-delay stage: 500 updates, validation every 250, learning rate 0.0005, batch four, unroll 384. Binding/delay stage: 1,500 updates, validation every 500, same optimizer settings; initialize from basic development-selected checkpoint. Select only on the corresponding development target loss, with initial step zero eligible. Both architectures receive the same data/order/budget. Starting checkpoints are runs/memory-init-graph/initial.mlm and runs/memory-init-gru/initial.mlm, derived only from English. Do not warm-start from checkpoints chosen after inspecting old reading results.

Use 16 training, eight development and eight test names. Every synthetic training document must fit within one 384-byte unroll, preserving the gradient path from fact to answer. Mix 32 cached public training stories into binding training as explicit full-text rehearsal, and report measured retention; this does not guarantee preserved English. Basic stage has no rehearsal to isolate task learning.

Implement src/mlm/retrieval_data.py (offline generator/provenance), src/mlm/retrieval_eval.py (frozen scorer and diagnostics), tests/test_retrieval.py, and two configs. Retain existing data/models untouched. Prepare fresh data/retrieval-v1 with hashes and protect nonempty output paths. Tests verify deterministic preparation, no split overlap, labels/spans, balanced swaps/positions, exact delay, full-example unroll bounds, four-question grouping, and aggregation with deliberately wrong predictions. Run a smoke frozen evaluation before training. Freeze manifest/config/source hashes before training, then lock development-selected checkpoint hashes before opening test questions. No hyperparameter sweep.

Run both stages for both models; evaluate basic and binding development outcomes, then the locked final test and English retention. New task/test samples are untouched until final selection, but this remains one synthetic task and one seed, not confirmation of natural-language comprehension. Save failed probes and do not promote a checkpoint if broad quality regresses. Workspace has no git repository; save artifacts locally without a commit.

results/associative/report.md.text:
# Learned delta-memory architecture pilot

An opt-in key/value fast-state matrix is added to the fixed graph. This is inspired by [Linear Transformers Are Secretly Fast Weight Programmers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.11174) and the [DeltaNet parallelization paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.06484); it is not a new delta-rule invention, a complete paper reproduction or an optimized parallel kernel. The reference implementation is a dense sequential JAX scan.

## Mechanism and state contract

At each input byte, the existing graph produces pooled features. Learned projections of the current embedding and pooled graph features produce normalized key k, query q, tanh value v and sigmoid write gate beta. Read r=qᵀM_old; then correct the matrix with M_new=M_old+beta*k*(v−kᵀM_old)ᵀ. The old-matrix read contributes gain*(r@W_out) before the existing output normalization/head. gain initializes to zero. Querying before writing excludes the current write; predictions still use the current byte through graph features and predict the following byte. No future input, entity parser, factual metadata, string answer lookup or label-driven gate is used in inference.

The matrix is transient document-local state, not persistent parameter learning during chat. It resets with the GRU state at document boundaries. Invalid padding freezes the complete previous packed state, even when reset is true. State carries across chunks; graph routing sees only actual GRU nodes, not memory rows. Overlapping learned addresses can interfere, so the matrix is not an exact symbolic dictionary.

| Variant | GRU nodes | Width | Matrix rows | Parameters | Persistent state bytes/sequence |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| graph (memory=none) | 8 | 64 | 0 | 368,270 | 2,048 |
| graph + delta | 8 | 64 | 16 | 384,784 | 6,144 |

Delta adds 16,514 parameters and triples persistent recurrent state. The packed layout is [B,nodes+memory_keys,width], with graph rows first and matrix rows last. The 16 matrix rows are not 16 extra GRUs or named linguistic experts. New memory tensors have their own optimizer role/rate. Config.memory defaults to none, preserving default parameter/state shapes; memory_keys defaults to 16 and memory_lr_scale to 1. Graph/sum readout is required for the delta option. Standard stream warm starts require matching memory settings; the dedicated experimental initializer may add source-preserving zero-gated parameters.

## Preflight and tests

Shared base tensors match exactly. Zero-gate eager predictions and graph state are bitwise identical. CPU packed-scan compilation changes rounding: the tiny fixture's maximum logit difference is 5.96e-7 and graph-state difference 3.73e-9. Compiled comparisons use 1e-6 tolerance; full-English initial loss difference must be ≤1e-5. Do not claim bitwise compiled equivalence between different state layouts.

Real-source initial English development loss: graph 1.352696033935, delta 1.352696040947; absolute difference 7.01e-09.


All 68 regression tests passed (178.86 seconds); 16 targeted checks passed (69.22 seconds). Tests cover orthogonal overwrite/read, overlapping addresses and fractional writes, finite/open-gate gradients into every memory tensor, nonzero first gradient at the zero output gate, prefix causality, chunk equivalence, reset/padding, true-node route shape, effective memory update scaling including decay, and exact checkpoint/CLI stream continuation. A populated legacy checkpoint omits the new settings and continues with default behavior. Separate review found three test gaps; all were addressed and the follow-up review has no unresolved findings. Ruff lint/format and source type checks passed.

## Frozen architecture comparison

Both variants independently adapt the same preserved English-only hierarchical checkpoint, with fresh optimizers, seed 42, batch 4/unroll 128 and 2,000 QA + 2,000 English rehearsal updates. Shared representation rate is 0.0003; node/router/memory rates are 0.003. A new transfer_data seed 638101 snapshot provides 128 diverse training groups on 16 labels. Both arms receive exactly the same facts, queries, sampling trace, supervision and English stream. The generator also creates fixed/mixed pools, but neither is trained in this pilot.

These are fixed endpoints, not development-selected checkpoints. Initial functions match numerically due to the zero output gate, avoiding a large inherited-function mismatch. The memory model still has extra parameters, state and compute: this is a source-preserving adaptation pilot, not a parameter/state-matched proof, matched English pretraining from scratch, an inference-time online learning result or an architectural superiority claim. All Adam moments are deliberately reset in both arms.

Training acquisition/retention requires ≥87.5% complete training groups and English-dev loss ≤1.25×source. A training group has four assignment/query conditions. Fresh-test reliable transfer requires ≥90% complete cases in every bucket, including both fact orders (eight conditions). Six test buckets cross familiar-name/new-pair versus new-name labels with base, alternate and heldout wording. Each has 48 cases; total 288 cases/2,304 questions. Only base rendering is trained in this pilot. Task-level novelty is not global novelty relative to English pretraining. Test scoring starts only after all final hashes are locked; the repeatedly used English test is not reopened.

## Acquisition and English retention

| Variant | Training answers correct | Complete training groups | English dev loss | Joint diagnostic gate |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| none | 255/512 | 0/128 | 1.296104 | fails |
| delta | 265/512 | 0/128 | 1.291094 | fails |

Final learned memory output gain: 0.02116. A nonzero gain or changed memory parameters is an optimization diagnostic, not proof of effective memory use or correct entity binding. Raw fixed training samples and per-role parameter-change norms are preserved.

## Fresh locked test

| Checkpoint | Familiar/base | Familiar/alternate | Familiar/heldout | New/base | New/alternate | New/heldout | Complete total | Answer ranking accuracy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| source | 0/48 | 0/48 | 0/48 | 0/48 | 0/48 | 0/48 | 0/288 | 50.043% |
| none | 0/48 | 0/48 | 0/48 | 0/48 | 0/48 | 0/48 | 0/288 | 50.608% |
| delta | 0/48 | 0/48 | 0/48 | 0/48 | 0/48 | 0/48 | 0/288 | 50.868% |

These are neural likelihood rankings over two candidate colors. Free generation is additionally preserved for the preselected first four questions per bucket (24 examples per trained endpoint), at most 12 bytes each, using strip/casefold grading without extraction/repair. This is not a broad chat or complete free-generation benchmark. Within/cross-role test strata and raw scores are included. Offline roles, facts and correct indices never act as an inference solver.

## Cost measurement

Every arm uses 2,000 QA + 2,000 English updates, 40,000 supervised QA payload bytes and the same English-stream coverage. Matched update count does not imply equal FLOPs or wall time. Both endpoints are timed sequentially in fresh CPU processes after all training/evaluation workers finish: batch 1, fixed identical random byte inputs, 5 warmups and 30 repetitions, with compile/first forward separate.

| Variant | Forward length | Median ms | p95 ms | Compile + first forward seconds |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| none | 32 | 0.954 | 1.534 | 0.155 |
| none | 128 | 3.684 | 4.133 | 0.153 |
| none | 512 | 13.561 | 18.428 | 0.169 |
| delta | 32 | 1.023 | 1.378 | 0.209 |
| delta | 128 | 3.700 | 3.977 | 0.226 |
| delta | 512 | 15.700 | 16.558 | 0.227 |

| Variant | Parameter bytes | Optimizer tensor bytes | State bytes/sequence | Peak process RSS KiB |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| none | 1,473,080 | 2,946,164 | 2,048 | 377,024 |
| delta | 1,539,136 | 3,078,276 | 6,144 | 402,572 |

Timing is a warmed full forward, excluding text I/O and generation-loop costs. RSS includes checkpoint optimizer loading, JAX and compilation; it is not isolated inference RAM. The matrix has fixed size and uses dense operations. Neither these CPU figures nor recurrent state size establish any-device portability, sparse efficiency, Transformer replacement or scaling advantages.

## Interpretation and next gate

none: 0/288 complete fresh test cases; reliable-transfer gate not met.

delta: 0/288 complete fresh test cases; reliable-transfer gate not met.

The matrix mechanism is implemented and differentiable, but it does not demonstrate reliable binding at this budget. Algebraic storage tests assume supplied keys/values; the language model must still learn suitable encodings and write/read timing from byte-level loss. Added memory does not by itself teach that procedure. With 128 groups and only 15–16 presentations per group, exposure and optimization remain explanations. Preserve this negative result, diagnose learned addressing/write behavior and acquisition on small controlled sets before increasing memory size or depth.

No endpoint is promoted. Use fresh confirmation for any changes chosen after this test. The prototype still has fixed graph nodes and fixed memory dimensions; there is no growing expert web, assigned grammar categories, permanent self-learning during generation or proven Transformer replacement.

## Reproduction and artifacts

```sh
uv run python -m mlm.transfer_data --out data/kv-binding-new --seed 638101
uv run python -m mlm.plasticity_run --data data/kv-binding-new/diverse --config configs/associative-delta.json --init runs/scratch-english-hierarchical-v1/best.mlm --out runs/associative-delta-new --groups 128 --steps 2000 --rehearsal
```

Repeat with associative-none config and a fresh output path. Finish and lock all endpoints before model test scoring. protocol.json stores commands and frozen file hashes; preflight.json records source equivalence/state cost; checkpoint-lock.json precedes fresh tests; summary.json contains audits/outcomes; runtime-*.json contains raw timings/environment. Source/tests/config/lock snapshots have SHA256 hashes. Initial/final scored items, raw generation and full optimizer checkpoints remain archived. The runner has no resume CLI; generic checkpoint loading and standard full-stream continuation are tested. Standard stream warm starts reject mismatched memory settings.

results/addressing-replication/report.md.text:
# Fixed-source adaptation-seed replication

The four-group acquisition result did not replicate at the two additional predefined seeds. Delta scored8/16 (seed43) and9/16 (seed44) training rankings, with0/4 complete groups at each seed. Both graph controls scored8/16 and0/4 groups. The predefined delta acquisition gate fails:0/2 new seeds succeeded. English retention passes at both seeds for both models.

The earlier seed42 delta result remains16/16 and4/4, but it is a separately labeled, previously observed reference. It does not turn the new replication result into a success. These data show possible narrow acquisition with unstable outcomes under this adaptation setup, not reliable general binding.

## Predefined protocol

The [plan](plan.md) and [protocol](protocol.json) fixed seeds43/44, both model arms, and all budgets before training. Every trial starts from the same original English checkpoint with a fresh AdamW optimizer and the existing role rates. Each receives2,000QA+2,000English updates (4,000 optimizer updates per trial;16,000 total). Every training group is presented exactly500 times. No extension, replacement seed, checkpoint selection, ablation, new test scoring or model promotion occurred.

This is adaptation-seed replication, not independent pretraining. Shared graph tensors are copied exactly from the same English source at every seed. The seed changes QA group ordering and English document ordering; delta's additional memory parameters also change initialization. These factors vary together, so a failure cannot be assigned specifically to memory initialization, QA order or English rehearsal order. Within a seed, graph and delta receive identical QA order, byte budgets and English stream. Delta retains its extra16,514 parameters and matrix state, so this is not a parameter-count or compute-matched comparison.

The dataset remains16 aligned training records for Bon/Bom, two color pairs (gold/lime, blue/pink), both fact orders, complementary assignments and both queried entities. Metadata only grades outputs; neural inference is unchanged. The eight-condition tiny development case is reused exploratory data and no test file is opened.

The acquisition endpoint requires all16 candidate rankings and all4 complete training groups correct. The aggregate gate requires both new delta seeds to pass (2/2). A separate retention gate requires English development loss≤1.6908700424, which is1.25×source1.3526960339. Raw first-group samples and tiny development are secondary. All predefined trials stay in the denominator.

## New-seed results

| Adaptation seed | Memory | Training rankings | Complete groups | Fixed raw training samples | English dev loss |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 43 | none | 8/16 | 0/4 | 2/4 | 1.265716 |
| 43 | delta | 8/16 | 0/4 | 2/4 | 1.264488 |
| 44 | none | 8/16 | 0/4 | 2/4 | 1.255028 |
| 44 | delta | 9/16 | 0/4 | 2/4 | 1.256495 |

Both models pass retention at both seeds, with English losses lower than the original source on this reused development set. Acquisition successes are0/2 for graph and0/2 for delta; joint acquisition+retention successes are0/2 each. Delta's one additional correct ranking at seed44 does not complete a group and cannot establish a stable advantage.

Every new trial scores4/8 on the tiny development case,0/2 complete groups and0/1 complete eight-condition cases. All four fixed first-group raw generations score2/4 after strip/casefold, with no answer extraction or repair. The raw sample set is only four training prompts; it is not all16 generations or a chat benchmark.

For context only, the selected seed42 reference had graph8/16,0/4 groups,2/4 raw samples,English1.291641; delta16/16,4/4 groups,4/4 raw samples,English1.286896. Do not pool that observed success with the new seeds to claim the predefined replication gate passed. Two new seeds and a tiny task cannot estimate a general success rate or prove a capacity limit.

## Verification and reproducibility

All four frozen commands finished with exit0. The existing driver rejects nonfinite updates. The [audit](audit.json) verifies all74 frozen input hashes, runner identity, all four dataset groups and exactly500 presentations each, fresh initial optimizers,4000 steps in actual saved final states, config/counter agreement with actual checkpoints, exact shared source tensors and zero initial delta gate. Within each seed, QA order, byte counts and final English stream agree across models. Checkpoints, full scores, fixed raw samples, optimizer/source fingerprints, sampler histories, config and environment are stored under `runs/addressing-replication-{none,delta}-s{43,44}-v1`. Logs are alongside this report. The launcher refuses existing output directories.

Neural/training/test code did not change. The prior71-test passing result is the regression basis; the full suite was not rerun for this experiment. Fresh Ruff lint and ty checks passed for launcher/active analyzer; analyzer formatting passed. The frozen launcher retains a cosmetic blank-line formatting deviation noted in [verification](verification.json). Independent review found a completeness gap in the first analyzer draft; it was fixed to require16 questions and4 groups before freezing.

An optional type check later found ambiguous heterogeneous dictionary inference in the analyzer. The original is preserved as `analyze-frozen-v1.py`; the active version adds only an `Any` import and dictionary annotation. Normalized executable ASTs are identical and independent review confirmed no scoring/gate change. [Amendment](analysis-type-amendment.json) records hashes and timing. The experiment protocol and model code were not changed.

## Decision and next step

Do not promote the successful seed42 checkpoint as a reliable general model, or spend a fresh transfer test to imply acquisition is already stable. Preserve all failed and successful trials. The strongest supported conclusion is: document-local delta memory can participate in fitting this task, but that fit is not reproducible across these two new adaptation seeds.

Next, separate memory initialization from QA/rehearsal ordering in a predeclared factorial diagnostic while keeping source weights, data, learning rates and budgets fixed. This can distinguish an initialization problem from a schedule/order problem before selecting a learned addressing intervention. No new inference parser, category dictionary, hardcoded answers, node growth or Transformer-replacement claim follows from the current evidence.

# Memory initialization versus combined training schedule

For these two selected memory initializations, acquisition follows the combined training schedule. Both initializations reach16/16 training rankings and4/4 complete groups with schedule42; both reach8/16 and0/4 with schedule43. The new crossed run initialization43/schedule42 succeeds, while initialization42/schedule43 fails. Thus initialization43 can acquire the narrow task under the successful schedule.

This is an exploratory post-hoc completion of a2×2 table with reused historical diagonals, not independent replication or a general causal finding. QA ordering and English rehearsal document exposure/order still vary together. Generalization remains unestablished: every cell completes zero tiny development groups.

## Results

| Memory initialization | Combined schedule | Provenance | Training rankings | Complete training groups | Fixed raw training samples | English dev loss | Tiny dev rankings |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 42 | 42 | reused diagonal | 16/16 | 4/4 | 4/4 | 1.286896 | 4/8 |
| 42 | 43 | new crossed run | 8/16 | 0/4 | 2/4 | 1.270391 | 4/8 |
| 43 | 42 | new crossed run | 16/16 | 4/4 | 4/4 | 1.285907 | 3/8 |
| 43 | 43 | reused diagonal | 8/16 | 0/4 | 2/4 | 1.264488 | 4/8 |

Raw samples are only the fixed first training group, max12 generated bytes, graded by strip/casefold without extraction or repair. Candidate rankings cover all16 training questions. Both new runs pass the predefined retention threshold1.690870 (1.25×original English source loss1.352696). All cells complete0/2 groups and0/1 complete eight-condition case on the reused tiny development set. The new successful cross scores3/8 there, so training success has not become transfer success.

## Design and isolation

The reviewed [plan](plan.md), [revision2 protocol](protocol.json), configs, scripts and inputs were frozen before either new run. The first protocol draft was strengthened after review and before training, and remains as `protocol-before-review.json`; factor levels, budgets and contrasts did not change. The grid uses memory initialization seeds42/43 and combined schedule seeds42/43. These levels were chosen after observing the diagonal42/42 success and43/43 failure, so selection bias and historical/new execution limits remain explicit.

Memory initialization comes from each historical run's **step-zero** initial checkpoint, never its trained endpoint. The unchanged `warm_start` copies every tensor, including memory, into a fresh optimizer under the target schedule config. Every non-memory tensor (all graph/node/router/embedding/output parameters, not just the shared learning-rate role) exactly matches the same original English checkpoint. Seven added memory tensors have matching shapes, random kernels differ across initializations, and the memory output gain begins at zero. Preflight confirms every crossed initializer tensor and fresh optimizer state, and initial parameter fingerprints match their intended historical initialization.

The target config seed controls complete-group selection/order and the English stream (seed+1). All four groups are selected in every run, so QA membership is fixed. Schedule42 means QA RNG42 and English RNG43; schedule43 means QA RNG43 and English RNG44. English ordering changes which document bytes occur within the bounded budget as well as their order. It is a combined training schedule factor, not an isolated QA-order or replay-order factor.

Each new run independently receives2,000QA+2,000English updates,4000 optimizer steps, exactly500 presentations of every training group. New work totals8,000 optimizer updates. No budget extensions, replacement cells, checkpoint selection, new test files, trained readout ablation or model promotion occurred. Architecture, inference, optimizer, training-step math, scoring and dataset-generation code are unchanged. The task remains16 records for two names and two color pairs, both fact orders, both queries and complementary assignments.

## Descriptive contrasts

For complete-group fraction, schedule43 minus42 is−1.0 (−100 percentage points) at each tested initialization. The average initialization43-minus42 contrast is0; the difference-in-differences interaction is0. For question accuracy, the corresponding schedule contrast is−0.5 (−50 percentage points), with average initialization contrast0 and interaction0. Full within-level and averaged contrasts are in [summary.json](summary.json).

These numbers describe this selected table, with one run per cell. They are not population effects, significance tests or evidence that initialization never matters. For example, under schedule43, initialization42 has training query-flip fraction0.5 while initialization43 has0, despite identical question accuracy and zero complete groups. Their likelihoods and English losses differ too. Endpoint equality on acquisition metrics does not mean identical learning dynamics.

The supported lead is that combined schedule differences explain the observed acquisition pattern across these tested initializations. Neither the particular QA ordering nor the English rehearsal stream can be assigned as the individual cause. The prior two-seed replication gate remains failed; this conditional diagnostic does not retroactively turn it into robust acquisition.

## Verification

All203 frozen-input and endpoint checks passed. The audit verifies99 input hashes; full original-source graph tensors; every selected initial tensor; zero gate and fresh optimizer state; actual final checkpoint step/config/counters and finite parameters; exactly500 presentations/group; summary QA/English histories against saved checkpoint metadata; and full schedule, byte budget and English-stream identity against the reused run with the same schedule.

Artifact checks validate all frozen train/development question fields, derive predictions via argmax of finite saved neural scores and recompute correctness and metrics, and enforce the fixed four raw prompt IDs/text/expected answers. Preflight passed19 initializer/optimizer checks;10 clean/tampered-artifact checks accepted historical evidence and rejected missing questions or altered question/prediction/correctness fields. No model reevaluation of test data was needed.

Both new processes validate and record the actual frozen JAX precision/JIT settings and whitelisted execution environment before invoking the unchanged driver. Recorded source digest, Python/JAX/Flax/Optax versions, platform and CPU backend match both historical diagonals. The old artifacts did not capture numerical/thread flags, so complete historical/new execution equivalence cannot be proven. This remains a limitation when interpreting reused cells.

Fresh script Ruff lint/format and ty checks passed, and independent review closed all pretraining findings. Neural/training/test sources are hash-identical to the prior71-test passing diagnostic; that result is prior, and the full suite was not rerun for this experiment. Exact driver and child commands, execution-setting records, preflight, logs, configs, environment and full scores are saved. New checkpoints are under `runs/addressing-factorial-i42-s43-v1` and `runs/addressing-factorial-i43-s42-v1`. Preserve existing outputs; the launcher requires fresh directories.

## Next step

Hold memory initialization fixed and separate QA RNG from English rehearsal RNG explicitly. The missing combinations are QA42/English44 and QA43/English43, against the observed QA42/English43 and QA43/English44 schedules. Add explicit experimental runner seed controls with legacy-default compatibility checks before such a run; keep model/training math unchanged and freeze budgets/metrics first. That will distinguish QA ordering from replay exposure/order for this task before selecting an architectural intervention. Further replication and separately frozen transfer tests remain necessary.

# Memory initialization versus combined schedule control

## Goal and design

Cross memory initialization seeds42/43 with schedule seeds42/43, using original-source-matched step-zero delta checkpoints. Prior cells42/42 (successful) and43/43 (failed) are reused exactly as observed, with explicit provenance. Run only the two missing cells42/43 and43/42, from fresh optimizers for2000QA+2000English each, four groups,500 presentations/group. This is an exploratory post-hoc factorial completion: factor levels were selected from observed outcomes. It is not an independent four-cell replication.

No neural, training, scoring, config-schema or dataset-generation source changes. Use unchanged plasticity_run and warm_start: its target config seed controls QA selection/order and English stream (seed+1); all trainable tensors including memory are copied from the saved initial source. Graph shared tensors in each initial source must exactly equal the original English checkpoint. No inference randomness exists beyond initial tensor creation, which is entirely overwritten in this setup. QA and English order remain bundled as one schedule factor; they are not isolated from each other here.

## Tasks

1. Preflight: load source initial42/43, confirm step0 and intended config seed, same parameter names/shapes, zero memory gain, source-exact shared graph tensors, differing memory initial tensors. For each cross-cell use actual warm_start to verify every tensor equals the selected initial checkpoint and optimizer state is fresh/zero. Compare config except seed to original diagonal schedule config. Preserve all original files.
2. Freeze hashes of source/checkpoint/data/config/model/test/lock and orchestration/audit scripts before training. Independently review. Run max2 concurrent crossed trials, no replacement, restart/extension, model promotion, new tests or checkpoint selection. Logs and all existing driver artifacts saved in distinct new run directories.
3. Audit actual initial/final checkpoint steps/config/counters, full tensor equality with selected source, source hash,16question/4group coverage, exact500/group exposure. QA sampler trace, English stream and byte budgets must equal the old diagonal for the same schedule. Saved initial fingerprints must equal the diagonal with the same initialization.
4. Report all four cells with existing-vs-new labels. Primary numeric endpoint is complete training-group fraction; secondary training question accuracy, fixed first-group raw outputs, English retention and reused tiny development. Acquisition requires16/16 and4/4; retention≤1.25×original English loss1.3526960339354908. Report descriptive init/schedule main contrasts averaged over these two levels and interaction (difference-in-differences); no p-values, population effect, independent replication or generalized causal claim.
5. Archive inputs, preflight, scripts, protocol, raw scores, checkpoints, endpoint audit and output hashes. Update research.md/prd.md/README. Prior71-test result remains explicitly prior; core code stays hash-identical. Fresh script static checks and actual-run audits verify this control.

## Interpretation

An apparent initialization/schedule pattern is conditional on this source, two observed factor levels and tiny task, with no within-cell replications. An interaction means a single factor does not explain the four cells additively. Even successful acquisition does not demonstrate transfer or growing neural capacity. No new test data or trained checkpoint ablation will be opened during this diagnostic.

# Four-group exposure control

The delta-memory model acquired all four training groups after the longer budget:16/16 correct candidate rankings,4/4 complete groups and4/4 fixed raw training samples. The graph control remained8/16 correct,0/4 complete groups and2/4 raw samples. Frozen removal of the fitted delta readout drops training accuracy to50% and complete groups to0/4. This is a positive small-set acquisition result, not general binding or evidence that MLM replaces Transformers.

## Fixed protocol

[Protocol](protocol.json) and [plan](plan.md) were saved before training. Two independent runs reuse the unchanged `mlm.plasticity_run` driver, original English-only checkpoint, fresh AdamW, seed42, batch4 and existing role-rate configs. Each receives2,000QA+2,000English updates (4,000 optimizer updates each;8,000 total). Every one of four groups is presented exactly500 times.

The dataset is the earlier16-record subset: Bon/Bom, two color pairs (gold/lime and blue/pink), both fact orders, both queried entities and complementary assignments. No new training data or inference rules were introduced. The tiny reused development case has eight conditions; no test files were opened. Assessment is at the fixed endpoint, with no best-checkpoint selection.

This matches QA presentations per group to the old single-group run but uses four times as many total updates and English rehearsal updates. Against the old four-group run, both QA exposure and rehearsal increase together. Therefore it cannot isolate additional QA exposure from rehearsal or total optimization. The graph/delta endpoint comparison matches data, updates, role rates for shared tensors and sampling, but delta adds16,514 parameters and matrix state; it is not a parameter-count or compute-matched comparison.

## Results

| Memory | Trial | QA presentations/group | Training accuracy | Complete groups | Fixed raw samples | English dev loss |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| none | 1 group;500 QA +500 English | 500 | 100% | 1/1 | 4/4 | 1.361780 |
| none | 4 groups;500 QA +500 English | 125 | 50% | 0/4 | 2/4 | 1.367070 |
| none | 4 groups;2000 QA +2000 English | 500 | 50% | 0/4 | 2/4 | 1.291641 |
| delta | 1 group;500 QA +500 English | 500 | 100% | 1/1 | 4/4 | 1.359972 |
| delta | 4 groups;500 QA +500 English | 125 | 50% | 0/4 | 2/4 | 1.363914 |
| delta | 4 groups;2000 QA +2000 English | 500 | 100% | 4/4 | 4/4 | 1.286896 |

All raw samples are the fixed first training group with max12 generated bytes, graded only by strip/casefold. Candidate rankings cover all16 training questions; raw generation does not cover all16. Delta emits gold/lime/lime/gold correctly. The graph emits `goodd`, `limen some s`, `lime`, `gold` after trimming newlines.

Both longer-budget models score4/8 questions and0/2 complete groups on the tiny reused development case (zero complete eight-condition cases). Delta development query-flip fraction is0.5, but this does not amount to successful transfer. English loss is1.291641 graph and1.286896 delta, compared with source1.352696. Retention improved on this reused development set, which cannot establish broad English quality.

The previous four-group500-update failure was a finite-budget observation, not proof that the architecture could never acquire these groups. The delta success now establishes learnability of this narrow set under this schedule. One seed and two names do not establish a general algorithm or a stable advantage across runs.

## Post-hoc memory-output check

After observing the fitted delta endpoint, we added an explicitly post-hoc, training-only [ablation](ablate.py). It copies frozen params and sets only `memory_gain=0`, with no retraining, file mutation or test scoring. Keys, queries, writes and graph computation still execute.

With output enabled, training accuracy is100%, context/query flips100% and complete groups4/4. With output disabled, accuracy is50%, flips0%, complete groups0/4;8 of16 predictions change. The fitted network depends on the memory output channel for this task. This does not show that the matrix implements a general entity dictionary or isolate the benefit of training with memory: the network is coadapted and has extra parameters. No raw disabled-readout generations or English ablation scores were computed in this check.

## Verification

The [endpoint audit](audit.json) verifies all72 frozen input hashes, exact budgets,500 presentations per group, fresh optimizer states, identical sampler prefixes/initial fingerprints/initial assessments/rate policies versus earlier short runs, identical shared initial graph parameters across models, zero initial memory gate, and matched sampler/byte budgets/English-stream state across the two new runs. The driver rejects nonfinite updates; both runs completed normally. Original sources and prior probe outputs remain unchanged.

Model, training, inference and test sources are unchanged from the prior71-test passing diagnostic. The suite was not rerun for this experiment; verification instead checks those source hashes, actual run completion, endpoint invariants and analysis-script lint/format. Independent protocol/audit review found no material gaps. Reproducibility commands are in the protocol; initial/final checkpoints, config, environment, counter and sampler histories and full neural scores are under `runs/addressing-exposure-{none,delta}-g4-v1`. Running the protocol again requires fresh output directories.

## Next step

Replicate this exact acquisition comparison with additional predefined seeds before changing the architecture or increasing the dataset substantially. If acquisition is stable, use a separately frozen transfer evaluation across different entity pairs, names and fact wording. Keep memorization and transfer separate, retain a graph control and report the memory parameter/state cost. No checkpoint is promoted as a general-purpose model by this experiment.

results/addressing/report.md.text:
# Learned-memory addressing diagnostic

The memory is active, but this experiment finds no reliable entity–color binding advantage. Both graph control and delta model memorize one group; both fail the four-group probe at this fixed budget. No architecture or training behavior changed, and no new test scores were computed.

## Protocol

The frozen [plan](../../addressing-plan.md) and [protocol](protocol.json) specify the analysis. The reproducible [recipe](recipe.py) uses the original English-only checkpoint independently for each trial, fresh AdamW, seed42, identical split role rates, batch4, 500 QA plus500 English updates. Four trials total4,000 optimizer updates. None starts from the failed pilot or another probe.

Training subsets are the first4 and16 records of the old diverse pool: one group (two assignments ×two queried entities), or four groups (same Bon/Bom pair, gold/lime and blue/pink, both fact orders). Tiny development is the first complete eight-condition case from the old development pool. It is exploratory and previously available, not a fresh test. Each one-group trial sees its group500 times; each four-group trial sees each group125 times. Therefore these probes do not isolate diversity, order reversal or exposure as causal factors. No checkpoint selection or promotion.

## Small-set results

Candidate ranking is the unchanged mean neural answer-byte likelihood scorer. Raw answers below use the fixed first training group and only strip/casefold normalization. They are training samples.

| Trial | Training questions correct | Complete training groups | Raw samples correct | English dev loss |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| addressing-none-g1-v1 | 100.00% | 1/1 | 4/4 | 1.361780 |
| addressing-delta-g1-v1 | 100.00% | 1/1 | 4/4 | 1.359972 |
| addressing-none-g4-v1 | 50.00% | 0/4 | 2/4 | 1.367070 |
| addressing-delta-g4-v1 | 50.00% | 0/4 | 2/4 | 1.363914 |

All probes complete zero of two tiny development groups. One-group raw success is memorization, not evidence of general binding or English chat readiness. Four-group failures at500 QA updates do not prove a capacity limit. English development losses are around1.36 versus1.352696 for the source; this is retention evidence on a reused development set.

## What the failed pilot memory learned

We traced the first eight original training prompts (one Bon/Bom gold/lime case, both fact orders), both before and after the earlier2,000QA+2,000English pilot. Prompt bytes alone enter the tracer. Facts/labels only annotate regions afterward; no symbolic lookup or answer repair enters inference.

The tracer reconstructs keys, queries, values, write gates, old-matrix reads, delta updates, pooled residuals and output logits from actual graph states. It checks token stepping against an uninstrumented full-prompt forward. For a read at t, the exact signed contribution of an earlier write s is beta_s × q_tᵀ A_(t−1)…A_(s+1) k_s × v_s, with A_j=I−beta_j k_j k_jᵀ. The backward algorithm excludes the current and all future writes. Coefficients can be negative; they are not attention probabilities.

Across the eight trained prompts, mean write gates were0.802 for fact1,0.885 for fact2,0.887 for the question and0.831 for the assistant header. Their initial values were roughly0.11–0.12. Mean absolute coefficient shares were14.71%,9.91%,43.29%,28.44% respectively, with the remainder BOS/user header. This statistic is conditional on the realized controller trajectory, not a probability or causal attribution.

The [projection analysis](project_regions.py) sums signed vectors within each region before applying the learned output kernel and gain. Mean projected region norms were0.1773 fact1,0.0747 fact2,0.0950 question and0.5708 assistant header. These norms do not add because region vectors can cancel. All initial projected contributions are exactly zero because the initial gain is zero. Region sums reconstruct the actual read and projected residual. Header/question writes can contain earlier factual information carried by the graph, so these measurements do not prove facts were erased.

Final query cosines for fixed-context entity swaps were0.9999717–0.9999768. Recalled-vector cosines were0.9794–0.9868. Mean projected residual/base-pooling norm ratio was0.08048 before layernorm. This is consistent with weak entity discrimination at the final read; similarity alone cannot prove why binding fails.

Maximum conditional-read reconstruction error on these eight trained pilot prompts was4.64e-07. Full traces, raw coefficients, values, reconstruction errors and query swaps are archived in the per-checkpoint JSON files. The residual decomposition is linear before layernorm; it is not a decomposition of final answer scores.

## Frozen readout ablation

Only memory_gain is set to zero in a copied parameter tree. No weights are retrained or written back. The graph/controller/matrix trajectory remains the same for fixed teacher-forced inputs; memory writes and their compute still execute. This tests dependence on a coadapted output channel, not the benefit of training without memory.

| Failed pilot metric | Readout on | Readout off |
|---|---:|---:|
| Training accuracy,512 questions | 51.7578% | 50% |
| Complete training groups | 0/128 | 0/128 |
| Assistant-target training loss, including newline/EOS | 0.123376 | 0.221659 |
| Mean correct-minus-wrong candidate score | 0.005023 | 0.000185 |
| English dev loss | 1.291094 | 1.289253 |

Nine training predictions flip. The memory improves training likelihood but does not solve binding. The loss and candidate-ranking metrics use different masks: training loss includes assistant answer/newline/EOS, while candidate scores include answer bytes only.

For the fitted one-group delta probe, all four training rankings stay correct with the readout disabled (zero flips), although target loss worsens0.001597→0.011597. The graph can support that fitted ranking without the memory output. For the four-group delta probe, two rankings flip, accuracy remains50%, and complete groups remain0/4; target loss worsens0.118962→0.307034. These results show active contribution without reliable binding.

## Verification and artifacts

The complete suite passed:71 tests in185.74s. New tests verify signed overwrite reconstruction, exclusion of current/future writes, actual/full-prompt equality, byte-region coverage and readout-ablation immutability. Ruff lint/format and ty checks passed for the new diagnostic helper/tests. Independent review found no helper issue and requested projected region contributions; the separate postprocessor implements those and passed follow-up review. No model, training, inference or dataset-generation algorithm changed.

Frozen inputs are checked in [integrity.json](integrity.json); all83 hashes from the earlier associative pilot also match [prior-input-integrity.json](prior-input-integrity.json). Source/config/test snapshots, protocol, logs, per-run source hashes, fresh optimizer fingerprints, sampler traces and counters are saved. Checkpoints and raw generations are under runs/addressing-*-v1. No original model files were overwritten.

## Next experiment

First separate exposure from diversity with a predeclared equal-exposure control, and retain the original source initialization. If exploring an addressing change, test one learned mechanism at a time: a controller that preserves the queried entity representation through the assistant header, or a more selective learned write gate. Keep keys/queries/writes learned from bytes, with no category dictionary, entity parser or label-driven routing. Compare against the unchanged graph at matched exposure and report training acquisition before fresh transfer testing.

This diagnostic does not validate growing nodes, category-specialized webs, sparse execution, broad language understanding or a Transformer replacement. It narrows the problem to learned addressing and acquisition under the present setup.

results/memory-retention/report.md.text:
# Retention-gate intervention

This experiment tests a targeted initialization change, not a new architecture. The fixed graph, state dimensions, learned equations, and parameter counts are unchanged. The offline initializer adds a bias toward slower retention, then normal gradient training can change all gates. Inference contains no response rules or answer lookup.

## Rationale and limits

For the implemented GRU convention, h' = z h + (1-z) candidate. At zero other preactivation, adding log(tau-1) gives z = 1-1/tau. We distribute nominal tau geometrically from 2 to 128, across eight graph nodes or 208 plain-GRU channels. We add these offsets to the pretrained biases, so actual input-dependent timescales are not fixed or guaranteed. The graph has repeated channels within each node; the GRU has a finer channel-level distribution. This is not an exactly identical prior distribution across architectures.

The motivation comes from [Tallec and Ollivier, Can recurrent neural networks warp time?](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.11188). Our deterministic pretrained-bias intervention is chrono-inspired, not a faithful reproduction of that paper's initialization method. Large retention gates can impair writing and gradient learning. Longer-lived state differences need not encode useful facts or support correct answer selection.

## Fixed protocol

Both models start from their respective 4,000-update English checkpoints with fresh optimizers and the bias intervention. They reuse assistant-v2, seed 42, batch size four, unroll 256, learning rate 0.0005, and 2,000 optimizer updates. Development target loss selects among steps 0, 500, 1,000, 1,500, and 2,000. No test split is supplied to training. Existing unmodified assistant-learning runs are the controls. There is no timescale sweep. File hashes are in protocol.json and source provenance accompanies each initialization.

The supervised dataset and old diagnostic have already informed project development. Reused test questions are therefore exploratory diagnostics; a positive result would need fresh held-out confirmation. One seed cannot establish a general advantage. Runtime contention prevents a controlled speed comparison.

The memory probe substitutes equal-byte-length green/white context facts while holding question and neutral filler fixed. It reports final recurrent-state separation and the change in green-versus-white likelihood margin. State separation is not a semantic-memory score. Positive margin effect is directionally appropriate for this single fact, but does not establish broad reading capability.

## Reproduction

Use fresh output paths; source checkpoints and prepared data must already exist.

```sh
uv run python -m mlm.memory_init runs/english-v1/best.mlm runs/memory-init-graph-new/initial.mlm
uv run mlm stream-train --train data/assistant-v2/train.jsonl --validation data/assistant-v2/validation.jsonl --config configs/assistant-graph.json --init runs/memory-init-graph-new/initial.mlm --out runs/memory-graph-new --steps 2000 --eval-every 500
uv run python -m mlm.supervised_eval runs/memory-graph-new/best.mlm --out results/memory-graph-new-evaluation.json
uv run python -m mlm.memory_probe runs/memory-graph-new/best.mlm --out results/memory-graph-new-probe.json
uv run mlm evaluate runs/memory-graph-new/best.mlm --data data/hf/stories/test.jsonl --full-documents
```

For the GRU substitute runs/baseline-gru/best.mlm, configs/assistant-gru.json, and fresh GRU output names. Initialization never modifies its source. Preserve the generated provenance JSON alongside the initial checkpoint.

## Results

Both models completed 2,000 updates and consumed exactly the controls' 915,785 input payload bytes and 82,737 supervised payload bytes. Final stream snapshots, training/development text identities, and supervision masks match the controls. Source/data/config hashes were verified. Graph selection chose step 2,000; GRU chose step 500. Later GRU development loss worsened; final weights were not substituted for best.

| Measure | Graph control | Graph retention | GRU control | GRU retention |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Best development target loss | 0.268223 | 0.278613 | 0.386889 | 0.401177 |
| Test target loss | 0.234342 | 0.230059 | 0.244349 | 0.281644 |
| Individual reading correct /128 | 64 | 66 | 64 | 62 |
| Complete reading pairs correct /64 | 0 | 19 | 0 | 2 |
| Preferred-answer changes /64 | 0 | 36 | 0 | 6 |
| Story test loss | 1.267662 | 1.849269 | 1.169831 | 1.855628 |

Lower losses are better. Target loss scores assistant spans and EOS, not all input bytes. The original English checkpoints' story losses were 1.121557 (graph) and 1.098890 (GRU). Neither new memory checkpoint should replace those English checkpoints.

The graph is now context-sensitive, but **reliable reading has not been demonstrated**. Of 64 pairs, 19 are both correct, 17 are both wrong, and 28 have one correct answer. The GRU has two both correct, four both wrong, and 58 with one correct. Individual accuracy remains around 50%. Independent fair random guesses would average 25% complete-pair accuracy; a fixed answer averages 50% individual and zero complete pairs on these balanced swaps. Thus 29.7% graph pair accuracy is not evidence of above-chance semantic understanding. Changes from fixed preferences must not be advertised as broad comprehension improvement.

On the original reused 24-question diagnostic, graph scores 15/24 individual and 3/12 complete pairs; GRU 14/24 and 2/12. These tiny previously inspected sets cannot establish generalization. On the fixed first 16 raw greedy probes, graph scores 6/16 and GRU 5/16. Unedited outputs remain in the evaluation JSON files; there is no answer extraction or repair.

## Memory observation

The retention initialization alone increases state separation for equal-length fact substitutions. After adaptation, graph relative state separation is 0.7602 with zero filler bytes and 0.05631 with 288 filler bytes, versus 0.002621 and about 2e-7 in the graph control. GRU shows a similar direction of change. This is numerical sensitivity, not a guarantee that the relevant entity/fact can be retrieved.

At zero and 36 filler bytes, the trained graph and GRU prefer the correct candidate in both green/white contexts in this one familiar-template probe. At 144 and 288 bytes, both lose at least one of the two correct preferences, despite nonzero state separation. The graph answer-margin context effect falls from 1.2822 to 0.02062 nats per answer byte by 288 filler bytes. This supports further work on retention and retrieval, without identifying a unique cause of broader reading failures.

## Decision and verification

Keep the intervention as an optional research tool. Do not promote these checkpoints to the default English/chat model. A next experiment should separately test learning to bind a fact to the queried entity using simple controlled retrieval tasks, then increase distractors and delay, while tracking English retention. Freeze new validation/test splits before further tuning; fresh confirmation is required. Growth is premature until useful retrieval has a measurable baseline.

All 36 tests passed in the full regression run. After strengthening metadata overwrite protection, the three focused initialization tests passed again; lint, formatting, and type checks also passed. Neural inference equations and parameter counts are unchanged. `memory_init.py` is offline only; `memory_probe.py` and answer labels are evaluation only.

results/memory-retention/protocol.md.text:
# Retention-gate warm-start experiment

Goal: test whether longer initial recurrent retention improves context-sensitive reading without adding state or parameters. Authorized as the next memory experiment. No runtime solver or topology change.

Design: copy each architecture's English checkpoint into a fresh optimizer state. Add log(tau-1) only to its learned retention-gate bias, with tau geometrically spaced from 2 to 128 bytes. Graph distributes tau across nodes, GRU across hidden channels. Since h'=z*h+(1-z)*candidate and z=sigmoid(log(tau-1))=1-1/tau at zero other input, this sets a nominal retention prior, not a guaranteed actual timescale. Existing trained gate contributions remain, so this is chrono-inspired bias intervention, not the original chrono initialization algorithm.

Source: Tallec and Ollivier, https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.11188 . Saturation/slow writing may harm learning; failure remains reportable.

1. Add offline `mlm.memory_init` with finite range validation, source hash/provenance, fresh optimizer, output protection, no mutation of source. Tests verify only retention slice changes for both architectures, source preservation, unchanged budget, and checkpoint roundtrip.
2. Prepare two initial checkpoints from the same English sources used by assistant-learning. Freeze protocol before training. Reuse assistant-v2 data, seed/configuration, 2,000 updates and validation every 500; no hyperparameter sweep. No test data enters training/selection. Original unmodified assistant runs remain controls.
3. Run both stages, score development-selected checkpoints using frozen reading evaluation, then measure story retention. Existing tests are reused diagnostic sets: results are exploratory and need fresh confirmation before a positive generalization claim.
4. Save raw artifacts and report including negative outcomes. Update research, PRD and usage. Verify tests, lint and types. No git commit: workspace has no repository.
